div.head: 297.—Thursday, January 8, 1852.
div.p: CHATELAINE.—Why have you not written again? If you direct as your last, the LETTER will be forwarded. Grandpapa has been very ill in town, and consequently unable to comply with your request.

div.head: 298.—Thursday, January 22, 1852.
div.p: HUKKY BOY CHARLIE CALL ME FOOL—me cane. Lizzy, pray come home. Your husband and sisters are reconciled. All is arranged. One of your sisters is waiting your return at Notting-Hill.

div.head: 299.—Wednesday, January 28, 1852.
div.p: LIZZY.—Your LETTER is RECEIVED. I am at Notting-Hill, waiting to see you. Pray, for the sake of all that’s dear to you, come to me, or I will come to you. Write at once, as I cannot return home till I have seen you. All are friends. All is secret as yet. Much has been effected for your comfort.

div.head: 300.—Monday, February 2, 1852.
div.p: S.lmpi F. npi npkl. B qkng. F. oimg a khq. 19th nhgm, oing. lqkh. hmig Fiffy mlgi, W. de W. 27th nhgm, mpkh. nmkq, C. qpoh F. khg mqho, lopn. oiph. omnl hipo. knq, qgh. M. g. re. & Bt-s-n S onpg C. qhnp F. oimg. niqm. npnih. npkl. C. qkin F. khq hlk, C hgo, F, qgli, K, F, mhik mik npqm, C. klmh, nhgq, Inho omgk, mgil B, hkq, S lmpi, C. klmh F. khq, hlk, C. qknp. F. qgli, K & B. . . l. . . r it is iklm. hiki qmkl. ogq. oqgp. to E lhmn, F, qogp. Sinm—J. de W.

div.head: 301.—Tuesday, February 10, 1852.
div.p: TIG tjvhw it tig jfhiiwola og tig psgvw.—F. D. N.

div.head: 302.—Thursday, February 19, 1852.
div.p: ZUTRAVEN.—WARUM KOMMT ST. P. NICHT?

div.head: 303.—Friday, February 20, 1852.
div.p: TO EQUATOR.—Fortuna audaces juvat—vincit omnia veritas.—E. W.

div.head: 304.—Friday, February 20, 1852.
div.p: M.D. M. C.—My position towards you is truly painful. It is now in your power to relieve my suffering? Will you when we meet again (soon I hope) kindly let me know? Jemius.—Wednesday.

div.head: 305.—Monday, February 23, 1852.
div.p: AUT CÆSAR aut NULLUS. Indigo blue is willing.

div.head: 306.—Tuesday, February 24, 1852.
div.p: MONITOR.—J. N.

div.head: 307.—Monday, March 1, 1852.
div.p: S.lmpi F. npi C. qgnl. F. npi, pink C. hgo, F. oing to E. nhkp S. mng to F. ilgn hlip, mo, olmh, mioq C. lnho, F. npi C. qgnl S o. g nq B klmh F pil qolg npi. C. qgnl, S mng F. qgli K. l...t F. qmkl B, qnp. F qgli, B. l...r C. lpi, F. oiph. S ognq C omqk y pil, B. hkq. F. inqg in F, hnio C iko S kgip, F, olhi E, nqlk F. nho, hnlo C, nolk, knhp. F. oing to mlgi mkhg qhnl F. lpqi iomg S. lmpi. J. de W.

div.head: 308.—Tuesday, March 2, 1852.
div.p: QUIS EST CÆSAR?—Do, pray, enlighten me. The agonizing week’s delay has not been occasioned by J . . . . S.

div.head: 309.—Wednesday, March 3, 1852.
div.p: TO F. D. N., Glasgow, February 16th, 1852.—“The Times is the Jefferies of the Press.” Beta, box 318, Post-office, Bristol.

div.head: 310.—Monday, March 8, 1852.
div.p: CIRCUMSPICE.—Box-moor, Herts.—E. W.

div.head: 311.—Tuesday, March 9, 1852.
div.p: R——. Thank you for the INFORMATION given a few months ago, respecting the letters sent to P . . . . . r. Write by to-morrow’s post, please. Fear not.—London-wall. Tom. Try to understand this mystery, 10.

div.head: 312.—Tuesday, March 9, 1852.
div.p: TO EQUATOR.—Circumspice.—Your great ship, the Christopher Columbus, when laden with indigo, opium, or the most costly merchandise of the East, never contained so much wealth as stands on that said hill.—E. W.

div.head: 313.—Wednesday, March 10, 1852.
div.p: INDIGO BLUE.—Where and how shall I send my address? I, too, have grown cautious at last. Are you as entirely ignorant as you seem? Be candid and careful as to this.

div.head: 314.—Thursday, March 11, 1852.
div.p: NOT to EQUATOR.—You might have saved yourself the trouble, and been the richer by 5s. Tom is sure to go to the wall without your telling him. The Ten is particularly happy, the chances being 10 to 1 that he will cross Earth’s central line, and then, being as invulnerable as Achilles, he will have nothing to fear. Tom will understand this mystery without trying.—E. W.

div.head: 315.—Friday, March 12, 1852.
div.p: AU SIMULACRE.—You have only precipitated your friends into the abyss of destruction. Ou pardonne à ceux que l’on méprise.—E. W.

div.head: 316.—Friday, March 12, 1852.
div.p: INDIGO BLUE.—Was I to say that my mind had not formed an idea of you, candour would indeed be wronged; but diffidence arises when I put this question; what claim have I to such kindness? Please send your address by letter to Alexis, Post-office, Chester; and, in order that the exchange may be mutual, my card will await you at the Post-office, Clifton, near Bristol.

div.head: 317.—Monday, March 15, 1852.
div.p: E.W.—What have I done to call forth such cruel remarks? Let me entreat you to favour me with some EXPLANATION. Enemies shall not long triumph over us if you will only join me in this declaration. Do not despair, or on any account give place to the dishonour of foes. In so far as I am concerned the matter has been confined to myself.—A. B. C.

div.head: 318.—Monday, March 15, 1852.
div.p: TO MY BELOVED EQUATOR.—When I visited the Great Exhibition I fancied Hampden, though refreshed with the living water from the Crystal Fountain, frowned at me; I hope our great countryman is now convinced we have not degenerated, and that his impersonation has resumed its accustomed serenity. Ce n’est que le premier pas qui coute, c’est fait; et c’en est fait d’eux. Vous voyez, la Providence n’est pas toujours avec les forts bataillons.—E. W.

div.head: 319.—Tuesday, March 16, 1852.
div.p: HONEST, HONEST ALEXIS! What a strange coincidence! Remove the last syllable, and there was, once, a great man, one of the self-constituted, sacred race, known by that cognomen, whom I,—for which, of course, I shall never be forgiven,—transformed—as I intend to serve many more—into a city spectre. Honest, honest Alexis! may that never be your fate. Candour would then indeed be wronged.—E. W.

div.head: 320.—Thursday, March 18, 1852.
div.p: E.W. by TELEGRAPH.—What are you alluding to? SEND YOUR ADDRESS. Direct immediately. I was much disappointed at not receiving it on Saturday, and have been in the greatest agony ever since. You are freely forgiven; extend your mercy to Alexis.

div.head: 321.—Friday, March 19, 1852.
div.p: IAM COME. I will wait but this day and to-morrow. Remember, “Now or never.”

div.head: 322.—Friday, March 19, 1852.
div.p: TO CHARYBDIS.—AGRICOLAE FILIUS WAITS.—Aut Terrae filius aut Fortunae filius.

div.head: 323.—Friday, March 19, 1852.
div.p: WHAT AM I ALLUDING TO? The Customs. You will only deceive the superficial fools of the nation—Alexis. A. B. C. & Telegraph being Siamese twins, the answer given to Alexis will do for the lot.—E. W.

div.head: 324.—Saturday, March 20, 1852.
div.p: DOOR-MAT and BEANS TO-NIGHT.

div.head: 325.—Tuesday, March 23, 1852.
div.p: E.W.—Author of anonymous correspondence, look at home. Conscience does not accuse me of even attempting to deceive. You have, however, been playing the game of deception for several years, until, judging from your exasperated feelings, you are at last tired that your bait has not taken. Have you a conscience? This is doubted by some, whilst others think that you have, but that it dwells far beneath its usual seat. Alexis bids you farewell.

div.head: 326.—Friday, March 26, 1852.
div.p: IT IS THE MAN—Yes, it is the man.

div.head: 327.—Wednesday, March 31, 1852.
div.p: OUI, je suis le serpent nourri dans votre sein; mais, pour le bien et peut être pour le bonheur de mon pays, et, quoique vous soyez de la race sacrée, il faut bien vous en souvenir, que mon sang ne soit pas l’eau de fossé.—E. W.

div.head: 328.—Thursday, April 1, 1852.
div.p: RESTITUTION.—The COMPOSITION will be ACCEPTED, and this will be considered final.

div.head: 329.—Friday, April 2, 1852.
div.p: S.lmpi C. qgnl. C. lnho, in (qo) F, qmkg C. okiq. E qlhp. C. nghq C. nhok. & klmh F, oqhi C. mgil F qik C. qgnl, C hgo C qgnl S. olqh. E nhkp. C nkh, B. qlpm F, kqno. F. oilg F, oqhi nohg 50th F, mlgi pgmq F, klgh ophg F, op B....ts. n., F, kmon C. mlon F, iokg 14th F, mnhq C. hngm K—t. F, hmig, F, lkhi pkmi, oqgp. S mnhk mnl F, mhn R——e F, komq F, mik. 711⁄2 N, 101 W. F. klih F, plmk gkmg S mihl D, olg.—J. de W.

div.head: 330.—Wednesday, April 7, 1852.
div.p: HARRY.—I said you were insane, when you wrote a portion of a letter which H. concluded. Your presence or address is required on urgent business. Write to the “Butterfly Seal,” or call upon me at F—— Street.—Harry the 2nd.

div.head: 331.—Saturday, April 24, 1852.
div.p: DOUBTFUL PRINCIPLES.—I entreat you to WRITE me the REAL TRUTH, or disgrace must fall on all here. I can bear no more.

div.head: 332.—Saturday, April 24, 1852.
div.p: BURY MY BONES.—BONES is earnestly requested to RETURN to his friends, and he shall immediately receive the remnant.

div.head: 333.—Tuesday, April 27, 1852.
div.p: DOUBTFUL Principles.—I by no means acknowledge this title. It is too bad of you. You are evidently laying to my charge things which I know not, and are crucifying me for the machinations of others. Where may I ADDRESS a Letter?

div.head: 334.—Thursday, April 29, 1852.
div.p: KITSY.—They wound deeply, but cannot destroy. You shall know all ere long.—April 28, 1852.

div.head: 335.—Saturday, May 1, 1852.
div.p: SOCIAL BRICKS, remember May 5th, at 6 p.m.

div.head: 336.—Saturday, May 1, 1852.
div.p: TUESDAY.—Quite correct. Quietly wrapt up in mystery and silk. I have seen it before mixed with others of different colour. One of the two letters you address answers the question of initials. Homage to the truth, to discretion.

div.head: 337.—Saturday, May 1, 1852.
div.p: S.lmpi at C. qgnl F. ikpg oinm pgmq 20th omp. hmip lqoh, hkom, hpgl kmhg, qik, lign. hoq hipo C. omgk B. hkq qkog &. F. ikpq qolg. in ikpg, mino, hmng okip, ikpg. khg to M. & P. pnog at hqon. hlkg nqlh. M. & P. C. nkh B. qlpm F. mp. C qonp. in F. mghk mgk at lgpq qik C qgnl & F hlnm, hqi C. mnq. F. oqgp kmon. omp 22d F. khmn B. . ts . . lgmh, oing npi qik C. hgo F. lgmh. oing to E nhkp F, ihpk hkoq C. iko S mki E mnqi B qglp F mik to E. nigm 1st F. mpqn B nlo. Fnipk C. ngil F. ongq lmgh.—J. de W.

div.head: 338.—Monday, May 3, 1852.
div.p: IKNOW the points of attack, but you need not fear. The parties who advance them do not know all. You shall. A true and (I doubt not) satisfactory account will be given you of everything.

div.head: 339.—Thursday, May 13, 1852.
div.p: EIGHTH MAY.—You are not despised—quite the contrary.

div.head: 340.—Friday, May 14, 1852.
div.p: EIGHTH MAY.—I feel delighted, and shall get mad with joy. Pray do ANSWER.

div.head: 341.—Saturday, May 15, 1852.
div.p: EIGHTH MAY.—Heed not yesterday’s device.

div.head: 342.—Monday, May 17, 1852.
div.p: AT SUCH an HOUR—at SUCH a PLACE. I cannot appoint until after the 20th.

div.head: 343.—Monday, May 17, 1852.
div.p: EIGHTH MAY.—The advertisement under this head on the 15th is not inserted by the same party as that of the 14th.

div.head: 344.—Monday, May 17, 1852.
div.p: EIGHTH MAY.—Remember my request of the 14th May. Say no more. Don’t heed other persons’ advices or devices.

div.head: 345.—Wednesday, May 19, 1852.
div.p: C.J.—Look for the third in my name. It is difficult for me to communicate through the medium of a newspaper. “Sincere Regard,” exquisite taste, but apparently no faith. I am not ungrateful. I only wish for your ADDRESS by to-morrow’s post.—J. 1851 to 1852.

div.head: 346.—Thursday, May 20-31, 1852.
div.p: AT SUCH an HOUR, at such a place, on Friday, the 21st, at 7 o’clock in the morning.

div.head: 347.—Thursday, May 20, 1852.
div.p: EIGHTH of MAY.—Will you write to identify the party? very anxious.

div.head: 348.—Tuesday, June 1, 1852.
div.p: S.lmpi at. F, npkl, C, lnho & inqo, F, nhmp., mqln, omnl F, hnio, C. hgo F, mik, the S, oqlg in, E. mgqk. F. qmkg iqhk by hnio, iom, B hkq F. npkl. C omgk. B hkq & F, qolg at, E, loqk B ogki F, oing nik hkom, C lnho. M & C qlin F. mik to E ng.qi P. to C. nhgq. C klmh at F npkl, all the hkpg. in lgiq hqon hkmn, oing lpqi to kpng hipo. C. qkin & the F. qolg, S, lmpi B. qkng, S. lmpi F. oimg the C. omkq. F, olhi qgli C. ngil.—J. de W.

div.head: 349.—Wednesday, June 2, 1852.
div.p: QUAL GIOJA per me é stato il rivederte. Ahiem? quasi ti credera perduta è per sempre.

div.head: 351.—Monday, June 7, 1852.
div.p: MARY HAMILTON. Wednesday, June 9, or Thursday, the 10th.

div.head: 352.—Tuesday, June 8, 1852.
div.p: J.—Let the result be what it may, you, and others too, have what is asked of an individual under the initials W. S. If by this time you have only learned to extend kindness to another, instead of cruelty to me, I shall rest content, as some good will then have been derived.

div.head: 353.—Monday, June 14, 1852.
div.p: QUERIDA, Querida, je t’en prie de REPONDRE ne seras tu constant que contre moi.

div.head: 354.—Wednesday, June 16, 1852.
div.p: AMOR! Amor!—C’est bien en vain, le coeur était lié, qu’on affranchit la main.—Resurgam.—E. J. W.

div.head: 355.—Monday, June 21, 1852.
div.p: BOCAJ.—ALL’S WELL. A fearful blank in existence, caused by separation. Hope is the greatest consolation. Time alone will set all right. Keep up spirits for the sake of the ever-devoted one.—London, June 19, 1852.

div.head: 356.—Wednesday, June 23, 1852.
div.p: IAM AN ASS.—A letter is sent to your post-office, directed to my bird’s name.

div.head: 357.—Wednesday, June 23, 1852.
div.p: MY Stature gives no inch, I throw away, and my bosom’s lord sits lightly on his throne. Il faut qu’il finisse.—E. J. W.

div.head: 358.—Saturday, June 26-30, 1852.
div.p: E.A. S.—Nowley Rowley 4th and 7th.—July 3-22, Received.—The boat was locked; a letter was waiting. The hour was not named. London address, 19, Clifford Street, Bond Street. Hall and Exhibition. I wish to see you.

div.head: 359.—Tuesday, June 29, 1852.
div.p: YOUR GOOD FRIEND regrets the step you have taken. Can it not be recalled till an explanation be given? Your honour and happiness are most sincerely desired. Quant à moi, j’ai tout perdu par vous, je resterais content si c’étoit pour vous, mais cette satisfaction m’est refusée. Santé, biens, bonheur, touts departis. Soyez heureux. Bonne foi.

div.head: 360.—Thursday, July 1, 1852.
div.p: S.lmpi. F, npi C. qgnl & F, pil pink, C hgo & B hkq F. npi C qgnl. F, qmk, C. okiq & npki F, npqm too, C omgk (nhqk) B pikl F, oimg a mpko. khq. C hgo F. oimg an oph npgm for 3 mioq C klmh at F, npkl, B. mipn. F, npqm too, C omgk F, qolg & mik at E. loqk for 6. F, hmkp. ikpg Ex . . r . . t . . n. F oing olhi npog C holk F, nqgm ohiq mogk mqho olhi C. iko B qkng & F. qolg S lmpi. F. ihpg hkpg onpm. C. kgql F. mik, iomn hkom C qkin. F, oghm. hipo npkl. S mpqg.—J. de W.

div.head: 361.—Friday, July 2, 1852.
div.p: TO the + on the LETTER.—Believe nothing, except that the “Hair Chain” is and ever will be faithful. Courage.

div.head: 362.—Monday, July 5, 1852.
div.p: WHERE the Teuton intermixes with the slave, and three of Neptune’s great European tributaries have their source, and also vile man is restored by the revivifying powers of nature; there, clothed in humility, sits beauty enshrined in youthful loveliness. La fin ou la lutte—à toi toujours.—E. J. W.

div.head: 363.—Monday, July 5, 1852.
div.p: BOCAJ.—All’s well! Every day lessens the dreadful separation. Being obliged to agree with two dear tried friends, who saw the last, no other communication can appear, but future benefit will fully repay the present very great loss. Time and silence cannot part such faithfully attached hearts. Farewell! Keep up spirits for the sake of the ever-devoted one. All must end prosperously. July 3, 1852.

div.head: 364.—Tuesday, July 6, 1852.
div.p: K.W.—I am not changed. Why so unkind as to think so? But may not time and absence lead you to forget, beset as you will be by trials and temptations? Can you resolve to resist them? To remain firm and faithful to the end? Forget not past dangers. Have confidence in the future. Endure for a short time longer. Be cheerful; be happy; and be sure of the constant devotion of one who doats on you.

div.head: 365.—Wednesday, July 7, 1852.
div.p: WONDERFUL! Thy star in conjunction with mine against the great globe itself! nor Afric’s poisonous vapours, nor Asia’s caloric, nor America’s life-absorbing ether, nor Europa’s invigorating breezes—fortune’s sycophants, nor adversity’s treason—shall ever loose those sharp hooks of steel with which I clasp thee to my heart;—France’s terpsichorean votary, Rome’s javelined gladiator, and London’s belted champion, were never lighter of foot, nor stronger of nerve, than Fortune’s spoilt and favourite child.—E. J. W.

div.head: 366.—Friday, July 16, 1852.
div.p: IF the Writer is not mistaken, a certain party has been, is being, and will continue to be trifled with by others, so long as absence is preferred to presence.

div.head: 367.—Friday, July 16, 1852.
div.p: K.W.—How is it NO COMMUNICATION is received from Quebec upon points respecting which candour and openness were entreated, that no mistake might hereafter occur? You are besought to let nothing stand in the way of such an explanation. Let it be full, unreserved, sincere—and be sure the future must be happier to all parties by its being so. Conceal nothing. Express your wishes distinctly—fearlessly. Do not suffer those you love to act in the dark. If changed in any respect, hesitate not to say so. God bless you. Write as before.

div.head: 368.—Monday, July 19, 1852.
div.p: ABSENCE is NOT PREFERRED to PRESENCE. No, no. But I must know positively if this is from you. Then I should be only too glad to tell all immediately.

div.head: 369.—Monday, July 19, 1852.
div.p: NO CHANGE has TAKEN PLACE.—All that has been hitherto attempted has been with the view to furnish you with full particulars and a distinct account of position and prospects, but it can only be done personally. Adopt the means which have hitherto failed once more, and you shall be put in possession of all you desire to know. Soyez heureux, and hold fast the faith.—Wonderful—fragile not frail.

div.head: 370.—Wednesday, July 21, 1852.
div.p: ABSENCE—Presence.—The advertisement of the 16th (but no subsequent one, mark this) was from G., who has had more reasons than one for discontinuing a distant correspondence, on which no reliance could be placed, when a nearer one was without effect. He is sure you do not know all. The truth has been sacrificed; he does not say by whom, but not by him. To this mode of correspondence he bids adieu.

div.head: 371.—Wednesday, July 21, 1852.
div.p: K.K.—The welcome LETTER is at last RECEIVED. Let similar ones follow, but with more information, as promised and not sent. Be assured on the subject about which you are anxious. Be patient; and above all things be faithful to the deep trust reposed in you, and the reward you hope for will surely follow. The attendant is going there (B—n), and will serve the party you desire if possible. Have unlimited confidence on that party’s good wishes to you.

div.head: 372.—Saturday, July 24, 1852.
div.p: TO the COUNTERFEIT.—Continue, and fill the coffers of this leviathan. Like the statue wanting at the celebrated banquet, though absent, I am all the more present.—E. J. W.

div.head: 373.—Friday, July 30, 1852.
div.p: X.K.—Yes, it does; but not the same party. You have seen other friends, but do not tell me.

div.head: 374.—Saturday, July 31, 1852.
div.p: S.lmpi at. C. qgnl. F. pil, pink M. and P. Bhkq C qlin F. pil B. mipn F. npi. C qgnl, C hgo F. iomg mhno E ngkp F. omnl. iqhp ihno, C. nhgq in E. ngkp C klm at F, npkl. B qoil C mkop and F, npqo. qolg, iomn hkom npqo lgiq B omgk F, hlnm oinp to E lino. F, omnl a mioq C. hgo. F. lmoh hkom E mgqk. C. kmp C. hnol to be F mlgi pnmq to. B. qigk de W. C. C. lgmh in. F. hnio. S lmpi at C. lhmn.—J. de W.

div.head: 375.—Wednesday, August 4, 1852.
div.p: X.K.—There is NEWS. Be prompt as possible.

div.head: 376.—Monday, August 9, 1852.
div.p: SIND sie GEWESEN? Jung Frau.—Ja. You are under a false impression as to what your conduct should be. You should brave what you shrink from. Occupation is arranged. Sleep in your own bed as soon as you can.

div.head: 377.—Wednesday, August 11, 1852.
div.p: AERONOMIC. 1852.

div.head: 378.—Friday, August 13, 1852.
div.p: K.W.—All right as to K. Very kind—very satisfactory—much prized. Continue ever the same. Be cheerful, be happy. Look forward, banish despair; feel sure brighter hours are at hand. If doubts sometimes arise, it is because the interest felt is deep. Forgive, and—forget not.—Haste.

div.head: 379.—Wednesday, September 1, 1852.
div.p: S.lkqo za and C. mgil knhp F. npi C. qgnl. S lmpk F npi C mqn nolk F. mlgi S oglq C lnho omgk B qkng F, hnio mkiq Ede F. mlgi S lmgh Lolly F, iomg at B pmik C hgo. F iomg in C olpn nhgq & qkin F, hkom npmq F, olk oghm at F. npkl S pgkh M. S. ligm to F. hipo ogpm mioq C oplk D. r. . ll. at C qgnl F oihp igqh mlqn log C mqn and qgnl mqn F. okni oihp hmkp in E. nkmp D. . k. ns. Fiq hkom lpgh nlp.—Z. A.

div.head: 380.—Wednesday, September 1, 1852.
div.p: IT is enough: one man alone upon earth have I found noble. Away from me for ever. Cold heart and mean spirit, you have lost what millions—empires—could not have bought, but which a single word, trustfully and nobly spoken, might have made your own to all eternity. Yet are you forgiven; depart in peace; I rest in my Redeemer.

div.head: 381.—Saturday, September 4, 1852.
div.p: WHAT SURETY? Not my country’s dishonour. Wait until you are asked; you never were, and never will be.—E. J. W.

div.head: 382.—Thursday, September 16, 1852.
div.p: TO the COUNTERFEIT.—Pitied, pardoned, and invited to continue.—E. J. W.

div.head: 383.—Tuesday, September 21, 1852.
div.p: ANY intentions beyond those of the most sincere friendship, and of the greatest esteem, exist in the instance referred to only in the mind of “Suspense.”

div.head: 384.—Monday, October 4, 1852.
div.p: TO G.—I MAY NOT.—Sept. 30.

div.head: 385.—Tuesday, October 5, 1852.
div.p: BOSTON.—Nightingale.—NO NEWS, but to give me information, and assist if needful.—Oct. 4.

div.head: 386.—Wednesday, October 13, 1852.
div.p: TO MY BELOVED EQUATOR.—Circumspice. Praeteren censco, Carthaginem esse delendam. Serve the Queen; be just, and fear not; let all the ends thou aim’st at be thy country’s, thy God’s, and truth’s—then if thou fall’st, thou fall’st a blessed martyr. My country, my beloved country, nothing but my country.—E. J. W.

div.head: 387.—Monday, October 18, 1852.
div.p: ALA CROIX ROUGE. Il se fera. Soit. E. J. W.

div.head: 388.—Saturday, October 23, 1852.
div.p: LEB’ WOHL! To the pearl of the great eastern sea, the blue-eyed maid of Israel, who keeps watch near the impassable gate of dreary Scandinavia, you cost one great man his place, and will also cost a great many more their place—Leb’ Wohl!—E. J. W.

div.head: 389.—Tuesday, October 26, 1852.
div.p: TO my beloved EQUATOR.—Circumspice. Ungrateful Paris is dead; noble Achilles resuscitated, and no longer vulnerable, even in his heel, sits astride the Equator, and bids defiance, even on his own element, to great Neptune himself. On to the State affairs. “Domine, dirige nos.”—E. J. W.

div.head: 390.—Monday, November 1, 1852.
div.p: Slmpi at C. qgnl. F. pil pink C. klmh B qigk. F. qmlh to Roker, omnl ikpg hkoq C nhgq. & B qkim F. qmkg qmp, ikho mioq mp the B. qlpm F. olhi C ongh F. olq npi C qgnl lnho, F kol to be F lhok S oqln, the F. pkgo. C. pmlq F. pngk S. niql 14th F, npkq to be F. hpl. S. onkl, by the F. ignp of C ikgp. S. lmpi in F hnio & C lhma omgk F. qmkg omnl qoip C. knho F oing npkl.—J. de W.

div.head: 391.—Monday, November 1, 1852.
div.p: FLYBYNIGHT WANTS the ANCHOR. It was expected all last week, and will be every night this week. Come or write. Silence added to absence is a cruel and unnecessary torture.

div.head: 392.—Wednesday, November 3, 1852.
div.p: SINCE “FRIDAY MORNING” I Die hourly. Where are you, and when will you return?—J. S.

div.head: 393.—Thursday, November 4, 1852.
div.p: ALA CROIX ROUGE.—Victoire. C’est fait. Soit. “Dieu me la donne, et gure à qui la touche.”—E. J. W.

div.head: 394.—Friday, November 5, 1852.
div.p: CIRCUMSPICE.—Corruption falls or I fall. “Il est trop tard.”—E. J. W.

div.head: 395.—Monday, November 8, 1852.
div.p: MY STAR AGAINST the ENTIRE WORLD! Neither the golden mountain nor the choicest beauty of Circassia shall ever sway my allegiance to my country. Richelieu. The pillars of corruption shall fall.—E. J. W.

div.head: 396.—Wednesday, November 10, 1852.
div.p: FLYBYNIGHT WANTS the ANCHOR.—My dearest friend, you have solved this problem wrongly, and are like Sisogenes, who made the error in the Julian Calendar, which led to very ridiculous results. I will now play Pope Gregory the 13th with you and set you right. Pride clothed in humility was merely a means to an end—the reintegration of outraged justice and the re-adjustment of her scales—and that end will be accomplished.—E. J. W.

div.head: 397.—Thursday, November 11, 1852.
div.p: FLYBYNIGHT WANTS the ANCHOR. A kingfisher has stolen the Ring of it, and Flybynight will founder.—E. J. W.

div.head: 398.—Friday, November 12, 1852.
div.p: VENTRE-à-TERRE.—Robb——o. Pardon. Thanks. Prove this false.—“Tis hard to wine and thrive both in a year.”—S.

div.head: 399.—Monday, November 15, 1852.
div.p: FLYBYNIGHT WANTS the ANCHOR. My dearest friend, the meanest garret in my native place, the eternal city, mighty London, is dearer to me than any palace, from the purple waves of the Mediterranean to the murky atmosphere of the Baltic. Pride, clothed in humility, though gifted with the beautiful eyes of Napoleon, on the same degree of longitude that made his fire new-stamped honour pass current, and though possessed of Aladdin’s wonderful lamp, will never sway me from my allegiance to my country—Richelieu. The pillars of corruption must fall.—E. J. W.

div.head: 400.—Tuesday, November 16, 1852.
div.p: FLYBYNIGHT WANTS the ANCHOR.—Solution—Invincible Achilles has pinioned great Neptune to the Equator, seized his trident, and with his triumphal car skimmed the boundless expanse of waters to hold communion with the Pearl of the great Eastern sea; Scandinavia’s gate has been repassed, and he now steers direct for the Pillars of Hercules: after razing corrupt and perfidious Troy to the ground, he will glide over the purple waves of the tideless sea, and pass in safety between the dreaded whirlpool and the six-headed monster—then, and not till then, the Kingfisher will restore the stolen ring, and honest pride, clothed in humility, and beauty enshrined in youthful loveliness, will be his ultimate reward! La lutte et (est) la fin.—E. J. W.

div.head: 401.—Friday, November 26, 1852.
div.p: ADVERTISE NO MORE.—November past, I came to London.—E. J. W.

div.head: 402.—Wednesday, December 1, 1852.
div.p: Slmpi at F. npkl, hoq. pgki C. nhgq is a F. hlkp no. F. mogh. B qkln F. pngk at C pmkg. on the 9th F. lgkh qmp. a mogk noil C nhgq is at C. qgnl. F. lgiq hoq khqp is oing to mpkh with C, qknp omgk hgo & kimh are F qmlh to C, qgnl for F qoip Fiffy. F, ngli oimg, a mpko, qolg hlk. C. ngqp. M. F. pgqn oghm to nqkg olhi hipo B qkm C. of F. hopn hkig pngk on the 21st mpmh hlko in C nkol.—J. de W.

div.head: 403.—Tuesday, December 21, 1852.
div.p: S.—NO.—She will be out for six weeks. Have full faith and confidence, and your reward shall be reaped.

div.head: 404.—Wednesday, December 22, 1852.
div.p: HEUREUX malheureux que je suis—I ain’t got not no money.—E. J. W.

div.head: 405.—Saturday, January 1, 1853.
div.p: S.lmpi F. npi npil pil pink. C. klmh, F. oimg ogq. khq lqkh ikpg ogqi, lqoi qoin oing lqkh, hmig C, omgk F, npi npil qmk. div.head: 406.—Monday, January 10, 1853.
div.p: QUELLE JOURNÉE!—The proudest day of my life. He looked! ah! how did he look? Like a man I visited two years ago in N——e. Tu comprendras.—E. J. W.

div.head: 407.—Wednesday, January 12, 1853.
div.p: IT WON’T DO, I’m a true patriot.—E. J. W.

div.head: 408.—Friday, January 14, 1853.
div.p: IF E. J. W. did not oppose Mary (alias Emily) Pierce Crawford, daughter of Daniel Mereweather Ford, he would have applied, ere this, at 4, Spring-place, Black Lion lane, Hammersmith. A wilful error is maintained against justice, however, and truth to oppose my right. Why not come immediately?

div.head: 409.—Saturday, January 15. 1853.
div.p: SILENCE!

div.head: 410.—Tuesday, January 18, 1853.
div.p: SILENCE, Where?

div.head: 411.—Wednesday, January 19, 1853.
div.p: WHERE? Has my mission been fulfilled, or does vice prevail! That is the question.—E. J. W.

div.head: 412.—Wednesday, January 19, 1853.
div.p: SILENCE, WHERE! Why! “Silence in the Metropolis:” Silence on the railway is good, but “Silence in the Metropolis,” remember, is excessively better.

div.head: 413.—Friday, January 21, 1853.
div.p: INCORRUPTIBLE.—E. J. W.

div.head: 414.—Tuesday, January 25, 1853.
div.p: DIOGENES his LANTERN NEEDS NO MORE; An honest man is found, the search is o’er. Incorruptible.—E. J. W.

div.head: 415.—Tuesday, January 25, 1853.
div.p: ALPHA the First, and GEORGE are Deceived. No mission but that of misery and ruin has ever been fulfilled. ’Tis cruel to add falsehood to injuries. Nor have I ever granted a person power to act for me. Incorruptible innocence need not shun the light.—Mary Emily, Hammersmith.

div.head: 416.—Wednesday, January 26, 1853.
div.p: THE KEY.—It is, and ever was, the favourite of the upright merchant Prince, not the prude of the coarse knight of the shuttle. Now you have my real motive of action—“blighted happiness.” Incorruptible.—E. J. W.

div.head: 417.—Thursday, January 27, 1853.
div.p: ALA CROIX ROUGE.—Victoire; c’est fait; soit. Que nos destinées s’accomplissent. Incorruptible.—E. J. W.

div.head: 418.—Friday, January 28, 1853.
div.p: CORRUPTION’S Dead; the victory is ours. “Virtue no longer of vice shall pardon beg.” Incorruptible.—E. J. W.

div.head: 419.—Monday, January 31, 1853.
div.p: LE JEU est MORT; vive le jeu.—E. J. W.

div.head: 420.—Tuesday, February 1, 1853.
div.p: S.lmpi ongm, kgip C. omkp. F. hlqn. oqhi E. qlhp. C. qknp. F. klmh khq oing a lgns. F, qoip. nvgm, C. qknp F, kpom lphk, C, nkim, hqn F, hkom. C, kioq F. oimn. C omgk, F, lnqh qlnk E—nkmp C, nhgq F, oing hnio, S. oqlp C. okiq F, oimg B. k. F lmqi C. phno.—A. C. B.

div.head: 422.—Thursday, February 3, 1853.
div.p: TO the HERCULEAN PILLAR (37), or Alpha the First.—The PAPERS of 1843 and 6, destined for Mary Emily, daughter of Daniel Mereweather Ford, deceased, were INTERCEPTED and transferred to another. Insulting Oppression reigns to mislead, and is opposed to Justice and Truth. Apply at 4, Spring-place, Hammersmith.

div.head: 423.—Tuesday, February 8, 1853.
div.p: G—, Arthur, and E. J. W. are inexcusable in absenting themselves from the Two Indescribables. Do not leave under a wilful delusion. Fear not. Apply personally at 4, Spring-place, Hammersmith. All communication is intercepted in England and abroad, and our reputations calumniated to render us homeless and friendless. Deceit prevails.

div.head: 424.—Friday, February 11, 1853.
div.p: ROSE.—Il. si. For. A. O. P. ⁎. 2 will not be too soon. Ed.

div.head: 425.—Friday, February 11, 1853.

div.head: 426.—Tuesday, February 15, 1853.
div.p: CENERENTOLA.—Until my heart is sick, have I tried to frame an explanation for you, but cannot. Silence is safest if the true cause is not suspected: if it is, all stories will be sifted to the bottom. Do remember our cousin’s first proposition. Think of it.—n pstb Dtz.

div.head: 427.—Friday, February 18-21, 1853.
div.p: SHE is RETURNED. But where is the fulfilment of those brilliant promises? Forgive past omissions, all shall be explained. Faith is in the ascendant. Write or indicate - +, if possible, before the 22nd, as I may be out a week.—Valentine. S.

div.head: 428.—Saturday, February 19, 1853.
div.p: CENERENTOLA.—What nonsense! Your cousin’s proposition is absurd. I have given an explanation—the true one—which has perfectly satisfied both parties—a thing which silence never could have effected. So no more such absurdity.

div.head: 429.—Tuesday, March 1, 1853.

F, hiqo hmng hnil lqlp iglp. omnl hkmi hkom noip ogk lqip hikl iom hopi iqhp.—A. C.

div.head: 430.—Tuesday, March 8, 1853.
div.p: TO my dear GRANDPAPA, of May 23, 1848.—Though held cordially tight, alas! no better did alight than the good man of 1848. Your child you loved so well is in great anxiety, and implores you to grant her an INTERVIEW. Address immediately, in her own name, at Standly’s, 61, Post-office, Brook-street, Bond-street.

div.head: 431.—Thursday, March 24, 1853.
div.p: FLYBYNIGHT has GOT the ANCHOR. Corruption wins, and England’s lost.—E. J. W.

div.head: 432.—Tuesday, March 29, 1853.
div.p: REPLIES to QUESTIONS;—Not going. Yes. Yes, if I possibly can. Yes. Yes; none.

div.head: 433.—Wednesday, March 30, 1853.
div.p: ACHILLES has GOT the LEVER. Corruption sinks, and virtue swims. E. J. W.

div.head: 434.—Friday, April 8, 1853.
div.p: F.G.—Mind not A., but remember B. Do not forget the silkworm’s tree. Think of China’s temples and of tea, of Hesperia’s sky and its blue sea.

div.head: 435.—Saturday, April 9, 1853.
div.p: HOFER was BETRAYED; Charette was betrayed; but God has protected me. I have fought the good fight; I have gained the good cause; now let me die.—Leb’ wohl. Adieu.—E. J. W.

div.head: 436.—Wednesday, April 13, 1853.
div.p: S.T. R.—Having had occasion to imagine that a very unwarrantable and most absurd accusation has arisen against a party, of attempting to personate some one of distinction, whom he decidedly never saw, and considering all things could serve but to bring upon him well-deserved ridicule. Should such an error exist, of course it gains consistency, and if only ideal, this will ultimately produce the desideratum (of re-establishing faith in the mind of the communicative party). “Silence has proved itself in this case not to be wisdom,” as only one honest word at the origin of this ridiculous delusion would have proved its fallacy and the prevalence of truth over slander. Communicate frankly by letter to X. Y. Z. 85, Borough High-street, Southwark.

div.head: 437.—Thursday, April 14, 1853.
div.p: M.N.—You are right in your conjecture, there is a difficulty. It may be necessary to lessen the time by a month. Write exactly what you feel on the subject; and arrange, if you can, for me to communicate direct. The name of your mercury will be sufficient.—S. T.

div.head: 438.—Thursday, April 14, 1853.
div.p: W.B. B.—How absurd it is of your parents to anger me, and to threaten me with law, when one word from you would answer every purpose. You cannot have received my letter of Saturday. How shameful to mistrust, you who have ever been so dutiful a child, and who now sacrifice your feelings to satisfy them.—W. B. B.

div.head: 439.—Saturday, April 16, 1853.
div.p: TO G.—The hope of one who could have sincerely perished for thee is utterly destroyed. The Unknown Admirer feels acutely the grief and pain the past must have occasioned in the mind of G. Forgive the past, and no more will be heard of the sincere Unknown Admirer.—Paris.

div.head: 440.—Thursday, April 21, 1853.
div.p: +VACILLATE Not; be true and faithful, and you will be rewarded. Any name which you give will be answered at poste restante.

div.head: 441.—Thursday, April 21, 1853.
div.p: S.T. R.—Second Appeal.—Would you play the philanthropist’s part, and act as mediator to remove that profound mystery which prevails (I think) equally on both sides? Not having heard of the nature of the fault imputed to me, I could not justify myself in publishing a denial to what possibly never existed. I anxiously await a candid explanation before I proceed, for in my state of doubt reason imposes silence, which oft-times is the evidence of guilt; but as you must be fully convinced that I could now have no motive in continuing the deception, whatever you may suppose me formerly to have had, state where letters can reach you. Address (as before) to X. Y. Z. W’s letter duly arrived, but the tone of it I cannot understand.

div.head: 442.—Saturday, April 30, 1853.
div.p: S.to W.—Your WIFE wishes to JOIN YOU, but must first know more. Your first letter is not received. You may trust me. It is out of the power of my friends to promise secrecy, others being concerned; but they will not voluntarily expose you to injury. H. has another important letter for you.

div.head: 443.—Monday, May 2, 1853.
div.p: H.V.— ——. My life is at your service. What would you have me to do?—April 30.

div.head: 444.—Friday, May 6, 1853.
div.p: ICLAIM the authorship, as I have daily and hourly renewed the oath, of that Symbol, through an interval of estrangement long enough to have effaced the inscription on my tomb. My altered abode you know, and the ordinary medium of communication is open to you.

div.head: 445.—Saturday, May 7, 1853.
div.p: ALEEKEPHALESKEPASTEER must WAIT—the summer is before him.

div.head: 446.—Monday, May 9, 1853.
div.p: WERE it my heart alone, let it break—others’ lot and misery are involved in “Aleekephaleskeepasteer”——Decision.

div.head: 447.—Tuesday, May 10, 1853.
div.p: ALEEKEPHALESKEPASTEER, compare the copy with the will in Doctor’s-commons.

div.head: 448.—Tuesday, May 10, 1853.
div.p: EXCELSIOR has PERISHED. The banner which he has borne for years with pride has fallen from his grasp,—its colours tarnished by a pestilential atmosphere. The ice has touched his heart, which will never thaw again.

div.head: 449.—Wednesday, May 11, 1853.
div.p: THE FUNERAL was a PRIVATE ONE. “Aleekephaleskepasteer.”

div.head: 450.—Wednesday, May 11, 1853.
div.p: C.A.—N 4 M S S—4 H Q O—T H M 40—M G—B A N N M E S O—4 A: P j—F S Q E—E S O N N—J A Q.—A S. May 9.

div.head: 451.—Thursday, May 12, 1853.
div.p: ALEEKEPHALESKEPASTEER—Your GUARDIAN is now in LONDON, but leaves for Genoa on the 18th proximo.

div.head: 452.—Friday, May 13, 1853.
div.p: THIS means of CORRESPONDENCE is both EXPENSIVE and MYSTERIOUS. I can neither afford the one, and I hate the other. “Aleekephaleskepasteer.”

div.head: 453.—Saturday, May 14, 1853.
div.p: ALEEKEPHALESKEPASTEER. See Mr. Melton at once, tell him all.

div.head: 454.—Monday, May 16, 1853.
div.p: ALL is EXPLAINED.—I have been to Regent-street, and seen Mr. Melton.—ALEEKEPHALESKEPASTEER.

div.head: 455.—Thursday, May 26, 1853.
div.p: IRELAND.—J.—May 10.

div.head: 458.—Thursday, June 9, 1853.
div.p: TO “ETIAMNUM IMMUTATUS, &c.,” de Maii 2 et Junii 1.—Vide responsa mea in “Tempora” Maii 6ti (“I claim,” &c.), 14th (“The Author, &c.”) et 20mi (“There can be, &c.”) Tunc tu scribe mihi, et ego rescribam. En onomatos mei grammata initiatia, ordine inverso.—E. R.

div.head: 459.—Monday, June 13, 1853.
div.p: JONATHAN, the son of Saul’s brother, WANTS his FATHER pressingly.—Portland-place.

div.head: 460.—Tuesday, June 21-24-29, 1853.
div.p: IF F. C. H. is living she is implored to WRITE.

lg.l: “And ever and anon of grief subdued

div.head: 461.—Wednesday, June 22-23, 1853.
div.p: SNATCH t. h. o. b. M. L. Roses. b. b. t. d. (Feb. 19.) WRITE in your own name. The obligation appreciated, and ever remembered. Advise and aid. Give the opportunity.

div.head: 462.—Friday, June 24, 1853.
div.p: WHAT you propose would be a most fatal step. Break off no engagements, but write and give me a safe address where I may send a letter.—Apollo.

div.head: 477.—Wednesday, August 31, 1853.
div.p: ZAMPA.—It came, and was as water in the Desert. Ten thousand thanks. All shall be done; but the time is long to wait. No more at present. The straw is in use. Look again in a week. Look always, and take heed. There will be no more until there is the return.—Adieu.

div.p: DO YOU REALLY THINK of the HELPLESS?—The drawing-room floor is ready; pray say the word, and the lawyers will be put to work, and provision made for you by an old friend for my sake; so cast your Saxon’s fears to the winds. Where do you draw? Alas! for the lost opportunity.—Edgware-road, 13th February.

div.p: FAULKNER-STREET.—Second RECEIVED.—I have racked my brain, but cannot for the life of me divine your object. Write again to unravel the mystery. “Hope deferred maketh the heart sick.”

div.p: TO NEMESIS.—I will CONTINUE; all the materials exist, but the labourer is worthy of his hire. I cannot run myself aground again, and must act like other men.—E. J. W.

div.head: 530.—Wednesday, July 26, 1854.
div.p: CARHEE.—Your letter on Saturday cast a dreadful gloom over all. M. would not leave that afternoon but on Sunday, and remains. Your friend will complete what you left unfinished at the smithy. All is mystery, and in coming events we anxiously await its explanation. The sympathy of all is with you. Write.

div.p: TO be KEPT TILL CALLED FOR.—Uccelletta! Uccellina! Alma mia dove sia? La tua canta, la tua canta dolce si tace! Aima mia, anima mia respondi! Il cavaliere del pennacchio bianco.—E. G. P. S. P. O. A.—Third insertion.

div.head: 559.—Friday, December 1, 1854.
div.p: GRAVESEND.—Key, as advised. A journey of observation may be useful. Keep a journal. Write every week. Do nothing without advice. Take care of yourself, and return when you think there is no place like home. All well.

div.head: 560.—Friday, December 1, 1854.
div.p: AIBARA.—Twwrdsp zzlm. Cntb atrck fthtb sefllw, ndnt yrwnd ngint dysppr.—Fgnne, rstssrd I lvfrunly, ndhpe ndfthin tme sstnm nmyprsnt wrte hdlnlnss.—Btdr stdrln gtrsr, srly “hnr” sntin vlvdin sndngm nelne drctn yrdrlylv dhnd Fthus urpl yptne wrdn nebt yrsl fedknw.

div.head: 561.—Friday, December 1, 1854.

C hgo F. hkmi ngmh E lipg C nhgq F hkom C ngqp okiq npki lnhm inqo mgil B hig C klmh B qigk 9 F, qolg C qkin lgi 3 F, qolg B qkng C mgil 5 F. qolg—npi ikpq lpkn npkl. F. pnki kpni lqoi ighp C lqgn ngml E mohn.—A. C.

div.head: 562.—Friday, December 8, 1854.
div.p: TO BE KEPT TILL CALLED FOR.—Great Portland-street. To A * * * E.—Sad, sad indeed! Your bidding and my honour are sacred—rely implicitly. But your friend who received your letters on Friday last will surely not disregard my sorrow, my anxiety. Her attention is urgently implored. Trust discretion.—Scordate! mai!—E. (Fourth insertion.)

div.head: 563.—Friday, December 15, 1854.
div.p: Slmpi. F. npi C qgnl. F. pil pink hipk nhpm pgnq kipo 1854. nhmp oim kqpo. hkom impq lmnp mqho oinq qgmk omnl hipo. M. P. C omgk qlin B hkq F. npkl. C klmh F. qolg qmlh qoin C ngoi F. oinq hnik C mkqn D. lni C hgo E lipg F. qik Sh . . w . . ls. F. mlgi ogln C qknp F. oghm. hipo S. mng.—A. C.

div.head: 564.—Saturday, December 16, 1854.
div.p: LA RUE de La TAMISE.—VENDRE—Vendre. Faut-il Vendre?—Egypte.

div.head: 565.—Friday, December 29, 1854.
div.p: LA POIRE est MURE.—Egypte.

div.head: 566.—Monday, January 1, 1855.
div.p: Slmpi F, npi. C qgnl F, pil pink ikpg nqkg S. ongm F. lqoi hipo ngli mohp ikmn lpgk milp ngmo qoin omnl 4 higo omp hmng olq mogk omnl. C hgo F, nhkp ihlm hog npi E hpg F, nhlp qmkg hmng olq oing hoqg ikph mlih hipo C lnho. inqo S. mhl pkqn. F, mpqn oqkh mohp qmkh S. knq F. hipk mqho pgnm. E lhpo. lqig 29th pghq B qigk C klmh 9. F. qolg F. npi C qgnl.—A. C.

div.head: 567.—Wednesday, January 3, 1855.
div.p: A.B. C.—I am shocked, distressed, and surprised. Address me in town, and say what it all means; and then, if prudent, I will see you.

div.head: 568.—Tuesday, January 9, 1855.
div.p: FRANK.—“I wrote in an awful hurry; called suddenly and urgently to L——n. Send a line there.” Impossible. No address inclosed. What J. and M. most feared has happened; therefore the third member of the triple alliance is summoned to the rescue on or before the 10th, to prove his honour and sincerity were not merely words. WRITE, and address as before.—January 4.

div.head: 569.—Monday, January 15, 1855.
div.p: S.lmpi. F. npi. C qgnl F. pil pink oimg hipk mqho. olhi. E lhpo. qik milp ogl—oghm hipo. M. P. C omgk hkq hkp qkng nhgq F. qmkn. E lipg F. mlih hipo C lnho. F. qmlh. lgmq S pkqg C okiq F. npi. E qlhp F. lopn hnkl. hipo npi. E. mpnl mqno. mhqp.—A. C.

div.head: 570.—Thursday, February 1, 1855.
div.p: Slmpi F. npi C qgnl. F. pil pink C ngil F. npqm C okiq lnho F. pqm hipo hlki. nqkg lqoi hopn npi ikpg oil. npi E lipg F. omnl hmng qik oiph hoqg ikph ikpg 12th lqoi mnhq kghl mlih hipo C mkqn iko F. kmn hmig C ngoi F. npi hmig.—A. C.

div.head: 572.—Saturday, February 17, 1855.
div.p: ROSA.—“Aus den Augen, Aber nicht aus dem Herz.”—Lui.

div.head: 573.—Thursday, February 22, 1855.
div.p: IWILL NOT ASSIST your INVENTION. You frequently convict yourself. Even the question you have now asked does so. Your concluding supposition is correct.

div.head: 574.—Friday, March 2, 1855.
div.p: YOU SEE quickly THINGS that you think you can safely say. There are many besides that, which you dare not mention. Remain in your heartlessness and selfishness, and with the conviction that it was never deserved.—R.

div.head: 575.—Saturday, March 3, 1855.
div.p: JE ne te vois pas, et je suis désolée.

div.head: 576.—Thursday, March 8, 1855.
div.p: JE ne te vois pas, et je suis désolé (e).

div.head: 577.—Thursday, March 8, 1855.
div.p: DO NOT be DESOLEE. I hope to have soon the pleasure of seeing you. Why don’t you write to me? I long to hear how you are. I am very well.

div.head: 578.—Monday, March 12, 1855.
div.p: ROSA.—Dant, vicl dant, gutig madchen von der blumen. (Es ist du wuste; nicht, als geliebt.)—L. G—S.

div.head: 579.—Thursday, March 15, 1855.
div.p: Slmpi C. qgnl F. hlin onqm hopn kgnp kgql omnl hipo mkhq lmhq lgpq nmkq oknh lmqi E. lipg M. P. C omgk nhgq B hkq hkp C hgo F. qik ogl omnl hipk oim hipo q.goh qmkg iklm iqhk lgon mkqp oing hlin mqkg klin qik lgnq. S pilh F. olhi. M. npi lkng E. mpnl—F. oimg hipk mqho olhi. B.ango—W.angée.—A. C. B.

div.head: 580.—Wednesday, April 4, 1855.
div.p: AUSTRALIA.—EMY, WRITE.—Toby.

div.head: 581.—Monday, April 9, 1855.
div.p: LA JUSTICE et sa BALANCE. Vogue la Galère. Egypte.

div.head: 582.—Monday, April 9, 1855.
div.p: IHAVE indeed coveted the possession of your letter, that I might R—d. M. L. &c.: therefore pray send it to me, at my own address, which you well know.—B. E. S., may I retain it until your return.

div.head: 583.—Friday, April 13-14-16-17-18-19, 1855.
div.p: EKEN BEZER.—All is yet quiet, and may be made right. Dives knows and yields all nobly, and will do more. Give an interview at once, and you will save yourself.

div.head: 584.—Tuesday, April 17, 1855.
div.p: J.K.—The landlord has taken all. Your wife and children are with me. I cannot see you. Let me know everything you have done, and what you intend doing.

div.head: 585.—Wednesday, April 18, 1855.
div.p: UNE fois pour toutes, veuillez me bien comprendre, je ne cherche pas a violenter vos dispositions, quand vous serez disposé à parler Anglais avec moi serai enchanté d’accéder à votre désir. Quant au cadeau dont vous m’avez parlé, vous me feriez de la peine d’exiger que je l’acceptasse. Le cadeau que j’estimerais le plus ce serait votre amitié; accordez-la moi, et j’en serai heureux.

div.head: 586.—Thursday, April 19, 1855.
div.p: CHUTE.—Honneur aux Braves. Guerre aux Voleurs. Vive la Reine.—Egypte.

div.head: 587.—Monday, April 30, 1855.
div.p: HOPE ON, Hope Ever.—Never fear my being able to achieve all that we can wish for before the expiration at which time three months is granted. Should you be uncomfortable do not hesitate. Keep your own counsel. Do not forget your D. nor our friend. Let me HEAR of you. Toujours la même.—W.E.E., 30th of April, 1855.

div.head: 588.—Tuesday, May 8, 1855.
div.p: WHITE LILAC, May 8, 1853 and 1854.—Esperance, Nil Desperandum. God bless you. The above is all left to me this year. I know not where you are.

div.head: 589.—Monday, May 14, 1855.
div.p: ROSE of ST. BRIDE’S.—Il appartient à l’homme d’errer, et à Dieu de pardonner.—W.alter.

div.head: 590.—Saturday, May 19-21-22, 1855.
div.p: A.Z.—The TOILET CLUB.

div.head: 591.—Tuesday, May 22, 1855.
div.p: ST. JAMES’S-STREET.—I tell you again I’ll not touch the money; it’s all stolen property. I can get an honest living, and I prefer such.—Egypt.

div.head: 592.—Tuesday, May 29, 1855.
div.p: Yunder Y 61814.—With many thanks.—C. C.

div.head: 593.—Thursday, May 31, 1855.
div.p: MANY HAPPY RETURNS of the DAY.—Send your address advertisement to the New York Herald. News of great importance.—Mayflower.

div.head: 594.—Wednesday, June 27, 1855.
div.p: TO ST. JAMES’S-STREET.—My ideas have undergone a complete revolution on that subject, and I tell you again I’ll not touch the money; it’s all stolen property. But where’s my child?—EGYPT.

div.head: 596.—Wednesday, July 4, 1855.
div.p: PAS UN MOT.—M. G.

div.head: 597.—Wednesday, July 4, 5, 1855.
div.p: JULY the FIFTH.—La première noce. Souviens-toi de la bague de malachite en fer-à-cheval? Ni oubliée ni pardonnée. Adesso e sempre.

div.head: 598.—Friday, July 13, 1855.
div.p: CARLETTO hat aus St. Anna lauter Eminenzen mitgebracht. Bravo, bravissimo.

div.head: 599.—Friday, July 27, 1855.
div.p: W.P.—You were SEEN LAST NIGHT. Hawks are abroad.—25th July.

div.head: 600.—Thursday, August 9, 1855.
div.p: HOPE.—Error does not cause anger.

div.head: 601.—Tuesday, August 21, 1855.
div.p: IVY LEAF.—NO ARRANGEMENT can be MADE until I have seen you. Perform the promise contained in your letter some time before the 30th of this month.—Δ. 7 = 2 = 11 B = 2 = 30.

div.head: 602.—Friday, August 31, and September 3-5, 1855.
div.p: AUSTRALIA—EMY—WRITE—TOBY.

div.head: 603.—Tuesday, September 11, 1855.
div.p: TH. a NI.—No 1, 2, m’est parvenu; je suis votre opinion sur la prudence.

div.head: 604.—Tuesday, Sept. 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 1855.
div.p: RECEIVED your LETTER with great pleasure, but with great regret for the pain you have suffered. What you desire so much would only keep alive the subject in your mind, besides would cause grave suspicions if discovered, and render nugatory all that has been done, which would be lamentable indeed. The other reason you mention has no influence whatever. Above all, to retrace your steps would be most unwise, rendering everything still more nugatory than in the other case. Consider the consequences and the pain which the sacrifices that have been made (but which do not suppose regretted), having been thrown away, would cause to others. I have gone away for five years for that reason. The initials had better be omitted, and I therefore do so. This will be copied by the lady you mention, and sent you as agreed upon. May God bless you always.

div.head: 605.—Friday, September 21, 1855.
div.p: L.—An entire MYSTERY, otherwise I would.—T. M. L.

div.head: 606.—Saturday, September 22, 1855.
div.p: TH—NI.—Mittwoch hab ich No. 4, erhalten am 17t. sandte ich Ihnen Briefe nach der leyten Direction. Ich bin bey M.P. Wenn ich wieder schriebe zeige ich es an.

div.head: 607.—Wednesday, September 26, 1855.
div.p: TH. NI., No. 5, ist SONNABEND AUGEKOMMEN; alle sind ruhig, und mit Ihnen einverstanden für die zeit. Kein Wort ist wahr von der Reise-Ruhe. Arduld und zeit allin wird Sugen bringen. Die Verleumder werden zur zeit die Stease finden.

div.head: 608.—Saturday, September 29, 1855.
div.p: PITY.—Yes.—The future of a buried heart and conscience! It is more than unfeeling to seize the unhappy hour of a weak and erring heart to influence it, to violate its whole nature, abandon the tenderest ties, and make it for ever bankrupt of every true and proper feeling. Remorse, and one day you will feel it.

div.head: 609.—Monday, October 1, 1855.
div.p: TH. NI.—Das Awiso B wird für Moutag benützt werden durch die versprochene bortsetzung des dennerstagiegen Briefs. B ald werden jene Wolken verschenchen die Jhren Himmel trüben—bliecken Sie mit zuversicht auf eine nahe Befreiung.

div.head: 610.—Thursday, October 4, 1855.
div.p: TO MY FRIEND.—L. 73⁄4 inches; C. 61⁄2 inches.

div.head: 611.—Thursday, October 4, 1855.
div.p: THIS is a funny world, and people seem to have entertained funny ideas.—The BROOCH was found to be of inferior description, and not likely to have been worn by either. The letter shall be called for if desired, but think better not.

div.head: 612.—Friday, October 5, 1855.
div.p: RECEIVED.—“It did relate to you.”—“It has reached the hands it was meant for.”—Your conjecture is right about the cause. I will explain; but in the meantime, WRITE to me in full confidence immediately you see this. I am very sad, and anxious to hear you know of who and what about. Address now M., Post-office, Camberwell-green.

div.head: 613.—Saturday, October 6, 1855.
div.p: J.B. R.—The MONKEY is HOME. Where is the Man of Ross.—G. G.

div.head: 614.—Saturday, October 6, 1855.
div.p: TH. NI.—No. 9, ist seit Dienstag in meiner Hand. Tausend Dank dafür. Mit allem einverstanden werden sie am 8t. die Autwort erhalten. Es mucht mich glucklich zu wissen das sie alle wohl sind. Nicht verzagen nur muthig hoffen.

div.head: 615.—Monday, October 8, 1855.
div.p: TH. NI.—In meiner gestrigen Anzeige sagte ich, am 8t. werden Sie Antwort erhalten, hegen Sie Keine Besorgnisse wenn dies erst am 10tm. sein wird. Ich beschäftige mich nur mit Ihnen, und Allem was Ihnen lieb ist.

div.head: 616.—Tuesday, October 9, 1855.
div.p: THE HALL.—RHOSLLANERCHRYGOG. U bi “This is the first time of asking.”

div.head: 617.—Saturday, October 13, 1855.
div.p: THE HALL.—RHOSLLANERCHRY GOG. Ubi? “This is the second time of asking.”

div.head: 618.—Saturday, October 13, 1855.
div.p: THE PRUSSIAN ALLIANCE.—Will any one inform the writer why we should be more angry with Prussia for not joining us in the war than with Sweden, Denmark, Austria, Belgium, Switzerland, and Spain? And why we may not have a family alliance with a despotic Power as well as a political one?—B. B., post-office, Chancery-lane.

div.head: 619.—Monday, October 15, 1855.
div.p: YES.—IMMOVABLE.

div.head: 620.—Monday, October 15, 1855.
div.p: BELL’ FIORE degli CARACCAS! Sera dell’pittore divino! Modella mia! sopra questo giorno felice ancor vi giuro eterna fede.—Vostro Poichè.

div.head: 621.—Thursday, October 18, 1855.
div.p: VERITAS.

div.head: 622.—Thursday, October 18, 1855.
div.p: BRIGHTON.—“I shall be —— months,” July 15. The proposal will be renewed when you return; its success depends upon your assisting me openly. Do write and tell me everything. I cannot.—August 12, September 21 and 26.

div.head: 623.—Friday, October 19, 1855.
div.p: M.T.—RECEIVED BOTH. You are very naughty. Pray do not encourage him. If you knew that your letters were safe would you write? My movements are uncertain just now.

div.head: 624.—Friday, October 19, 1855.
div.p: TH. NI.—Ich gehe erst heute Donnerstag nach B. um jides Missverstandniss vorzubengen sagen sie mir B. post-office, ob ich schon Mittwoch in B. einen Brif hätte haben sollen. L. Brief hat Al. erhalten.

div.head: 625.—Saturday, October 20, 1855.
div.p: K.C. B.—— V——Y. X.

div.head: 626.—Monday, October 22, 1855.
div.p: TH. Ni. Samstag. Haben Sie heute von mir Brief erhalten? Wenn ich diesz von Ihnen erfahren habe, nur dann Kann ich Ihnen wieder schreiben, ich habe vielleicht unrecht meiner Gouwernante zu miesztrauen, aber die Vorsicht gebiethet mir unsere Besprechung bis einer Nachricht von Ihnen zu unterlassen. Briefe nach London. W.—Ihre Mutter befindet sich besser.

div.head: 627.—Tuesday, October 23, 1855.
div.p: K.—Spare the undeserving. Transgressors there have been, ’tis true, but none so great I think as you.—A. Z.

div.head: 628.—Thursday, October 25, 1855.
div.p: JUDGE NOT that you be not judged. I am weak, probably you are strong. “I would not offend.”

div.head: 629.—Thursday, October 25, 1855.
div.p: HAYDEE.—Londres. J’ai reçu la visite No. 11, avec ses compagnons. Therese est très tranquille; elle approuve de son ami. Oui, je vous verrai comme vous m’indiquer; je dirai le jour; espère toujours, j’approuve tout; les ennuis cesseront, le tourment de Brighton est depuis deux mois à Paris ou l’ami F. la console; de Barcelone pas des nouvelles.

div.head: 630.—Thursday, November 1, 1855.
div.p: HOPE.—By that pure love I have struggled to preserve, with every effort of my soul; by that bitter cup you have given, and I drank to the dregs—by those ties no man can sever—by promises made to those now no more—I will see you. Be true to yourself and to me. Oh! M—y! M—y! I would save you the pangs of error—God forbid of crime—and though the passion, jealousy, hate and madness you have excited—be scorned and denied—when the serpent you foster is wearied—yea, even then—here is your haven, when all forsake.
God protect you.—D——.

div.head: 631.—Thursday, November 1, 1855.
div.p: HAYDEE.—Ce Lundi que j’ai reçu la visite de No. 3, elle était bien aimable, bien bonne, et m’a rendue tout contente. Par la même adresse vous pouvez me dire si mon ouvrage vous plait, je voudrais pour rien au monde travailler pour le Roi de Prusse.

div.head: 632.—Friday, November 2, 1855.
div.p: ST. PAUL’S-CROSS.—One thing you seem to have forgotten.

div.head: 633.—Friday, November 2, 1855.
div.p: THE gay flowers of summer we can but admire, but the wild flowers of spring will I place near my heart.

div.head: 634.—Saturday, November 3, 1855.
div.p: H.E. T. C. S.—Philip Augustus. “The oasis in the desert.”

div.head: 635.—Thursday, November 8, 1855.
div.p: D.—It must not be privately settled. You are deceived. Those now no more were deceived. I foster none: but am true to ties of happier days. Open to me a communication and a public investigation.—MARY.

div.head: 636.—Saturday, November 10, 1855.
div.p: STRANGER.—You were present, I was absent. I am present, you are absent. Suspense I cannot bear. Tell me, am I never to see you again?—W . . . . . r, November 7.

div.head: 637.—Wednesday, November 14, 1855.
div.p: YOU must be much more explicit for me to understand you. I fear a mistake in the identity. Give me some definition.—STRANGER.

div.head: 638.—Wednesday, November 14, 1855.
div.p: PUSSA, Hornsey.—Three sent with the initials—two to first post-office mentioned; the other to post-office, Knightsbridge. The same as ever, more so if possible. Gravels so nice; expected the weddings. April 29 and 30. P. S. Last just received. Yes, for ever——.

div.head: 639.—Thursday, November 15, 1855.
div.p: TO STRANGER (W. R.).—Met at the Adelphi, October 11; present also at Trinity Church, October 16.—M. D., 27, Jewin crescent.

div.head: 640.—Wednesday, November 21, 1855.
div.p: HEMINGTONE CHAUCER, C. E. Journal, 53, p. 32-128. —— G. Z.

div.head: 641.—Monday, November 26, 1855.
div.p: A.L . . . K.—Où puis j’adresser, afin que je puisse vous envoyer les cendres? COMMUNIQUEZ, comme autrefois, avec TOUT A VOUS—X. Y. Z.—November 23, 1855.

div.head: 642.—Wednesday, November 28, 1855.
div.p: THE ADMIRAL, Sir.—X. K. Y. Z. S. N. O. G.

div.head: 643.—Friday, November 30, 1855.
div.p: OLD ADMIRAL, E. G. C. S., 44, is in GREAT TROUBLE.—November 29, 1855.

div.head: 644.—Saturday, December 1, 1855.
div.p: THE ADMIRAL.—X. K. Y. Z. Mark, alas! I blame myself. Figaro has destroyed Prestos. Snooks’s “Old Clo,” hard up.

div.head: 645.—Tuesday, December 4, 1855.
div.p: A.B. C. D.—J’ai répondu à votre dernière lettre le 19e Novembre, en adressant 15, C.C., et n’ai rien entendu depuis. Il me semble qu’une lettre perdue ou un accident peuvent seul être cause de votre silence, et je suis très inquiète. Adressez, comme avant, E. S. R., etc.

div.head: 646.—Wednesday, December 5, 1855.
div.p: TO TOOOPSI.—L’orage ne doit pas briser la fleur; son gardien vit de son parfum et veille sur elle. Qu’elle ne se fâne pas pour lui—c’est sa prière journalière. Le bouton de rose voudrait bien être cueilli, mais qu’il se garde et ne s’épanouie que pour celui qui ne respire que par sa rosée.

div.head: 647.—Thursday, December 6, 1855.
div.p: THE ADMIRAL.—Not yet. Poor me! Sorry for Mark, glad as to the others. Anything pressing, say, and nw in a twinkle.

div.head: 648.—Thursday, December 6, 1855.
div.p: A.B. C. D.—J’ai répondu à votre dernière lettre le 19 Novembre, en adressant 15, C . . . C . . . . et n’ai rien entendu depuis. Il me semble qu’une lettre perdue ou un accident peuvent seul être cause de votre silence, et je suis très inquiète. Adressez comme avant, E. S. R., Post-office, Brompton-road.

div.head: 649.—Friday, December 7, 1855.
div.p: THE ADMIRAL.—X. K. Y. Z. L. N. O. G. Presto!

div.head: 650.—Tuesday, December 11, 1855.
div.p: INNUMERABLE KIND WISHES; ever true. Unalterable, unalterable.

div.head: 651.—Friday, December 14, 1855.
div.p: JENNY LIND’S NIGHTS.—Ladies and Gentlemen, TAKE CARE of your PROPERTY. A sufferer from the Swell Mob warns you!

div.head: 652.—Wednesday, December 19, 1855.
div.p: BOHEMIAN, where is thy work? For thee, all is delayed! Thou, who art called Target, WRITE at once to Newington-butts, and pacify the anxieties of Hookey and his clan.—December 18, 1855.

div.head: 653.—Monday, December 24, 1855.
div.p: OLD ADMIRAL.—E. G., C. S., 44, is in great TROUBLE. December 22, 1855.

div.head: 654.—Monday, December 24, 1855.
div.p: UNALTERABLE.—KIND WISHES. I have much to communicate. I don’t even know where the one referred is now residing. Left.

div.head: 655.—Tuesday, December 25, 1855.
div.p: UNALTERABLE.—KIND WISHES has been RECEIVED. The once referred is still here, and will be glad to hear a favourable report.—H., December 24, 1855.

div.head: 656.—Wednesday, December 26, 1855.
div.p: THE ADMIRAL.—Xkyz. Alas! Je vous souhaite une heureuse nouvelle année.
Requiescat in pace.

div.head: 657.—Thursday, December 27, 1855.
div.p: SPOONINI is anxious to HEAR of DAISY’S WHEREABOUTS. The charades pause for a reply.

div.head: 658.—Monday, December 31, 1855.
div.p: THE ADMIRAL.—Dieu Le benisse! Alas! tu dis? Je suis très inquiet; mille fois je réciproque les bons souhaits. Tu es mon rêve de la nuit, ma vision du matin. Requiescat in pace? Ah, que c’était Snooks.

div.head: 659.—Tuesday, January 1, 1856.
div.p: CE 1er JANVIER.—On vous renvoi à aujourd’hui un an le tout de même, hormis le refrain—dont on reconnaît la stupidité!

div.head: 660.—Tuesday, January 1, 1856.
div.p: SOMMES-NOUS toujours en rapport? Votre silence, nécessité ou volontiers? Depuis la réception des deux numéros, point des nouvelles.—Dec. 31, 1855.

div.head: 661.—Tuesday, January 1, 1856.
div.p: ALL RIGHT, to the 13th of October. C. is to be found at E., and protection. Murray will do, and possesses. Nos. 1 and 3 doubtful. Still depend confidently on the option William gave you; he will persevere through all. He wishes to hear from you much. Your brother is pretty well; his hope strong, and resolution unfaltering.

div.head: 662.—Tuesday, January 1, 1856.
div.p: M.D. is most affectionately thanked for kind wishes and kinder advice; but how sad and difficult a task will it prove to follow the latter. A selfish and weak heart has to be controlled, and its very idol to be given up. I will, however, strive as you desire, for I feel that I ought to do thus much at least for a newly found and very dearly beloved relative.

div.head: 663.—Wednesday, January 2, 1856.
div.p: DAISY feels inexpressibly flattered by Spoonini’s tender inquiries, but having found a more perfect hero in a new company, she begs gratefully to decline any renewal of the old engagement.

div.head: 664.—Friday, January 4, 1856.
div.p: C.B.—ALL WRONG, and very ill.

div.head: 665.—Friday, January 4, 1856.
div.p: THE ADMIRAL.—Merci. C’est le couleur de rose. Je suis malheureuse.—Presto.

div.head: 666.—Saturday, January 5, 1856.
div.p: COULEUR BRUNE et BLEU.—J’ai RECUE tous vos LETTRES. Mille remerciments. Vous trouverez mes nouvelles, comme vous m’indiquez, le Lundi ou Mardi prochain. Mon bonheur dépend de votre tranquillité, de votre santé; soignez-vous, donc, pour celui qui est à vous pour la vie.

div.head: 667.—Monday, January 7, 1856.
div.p: REACH.—YES. Address, as usual, W. H. C., 1, Long-lane. I mean the metaphors.

div.head: 668.—Tuesday, January 8, 1856.
div.p: THE ADMIRAL.—Presto.—Je ne veux pas que vous y aller à la Porte St. Martin. Vous la trouverez où je reçois la mienne. Demandez du Domino Noir, ou de la Blonde. J’ai tout commandé.

div.head: 669.—Wednesday, January 9, 1856.
div.p: THE ADMIRAL.—Do not send Presto to the Dominoes; it will not answer. Send to Porte St. Martin, to the name you first told me. Alas!

div.head: 670.—Friday, January 11, 1856.
div.p: THE ADMIRAL.—J’ai oublié tout-à-fait de l’envoyer. C’est absolument ma faute. On est fâché. W. W. Lundi—A la Porte St. Martin. J’attendrai la votre.

div.head: 671.—Saturday, January 12, 1856.
div.p: POETICUS.—Where are you now? 4, 126, 200, 272, 5, 96. Yours have not been received. Be just. TRUTH.

div.head: 672.—Tuesday, January 15, 1856.
div.p: FRANGIPANI.—Do not doubt me. Numbers 67, 412, 87. You will now comprehend the delay.

div.head: 673.—Tuesday, January 15, 1856.
div.p: H.B. M.—He that conquers a fault is even more worthy than if he had never erred. With truth and honour for your weapons—hope still.—ROYAL NAVY.

div.head: 674.—Tuesday, January 15, 1856.
div.p: THE ADMIRAL.—I have called twice. Presto was not at home. I cannot account for it. One awaits you at Porte St. Martin. Do not keep me longer in suspense. Alas! alas!

div.head: 675.—Wednesday, January 23, 1856.
div.p: LA COULEUR BRUNE et BLEU va RECEVOIR vos NOUVELLES; ils sont arriver hier, jour de mon absence de Londres. Je vous faire prévenir de ma réponse: je n’ai jamais d’autre souci.—19 Janvier.

div.head: 676.—Wednesday, January 23, 1856.
div.p: TOUJOURS en RAPPORT trouvera la musique à la même adresse qu’autre fois. Pas de nouvelles de Mama. Dois-je vendre les actions, et gardez jusqu’à quand la somme?—21 Janvier.

div.head: 677.—Friday, February 1, 1856.
div.p: BELFAST.—TRUTH.—He has, I expect, to receive a letter from her the early part of next week. Yours of the 19th came safe to hand. I was not so well pleased with the last entertainment.—B.

div.head: 678.—Saturday, February 2, 1856.
div.p: “Γνωθει Σεαυτογ.”

C.—If the advertiser is correct in assuming “C” to be the initial of the “author” of the poem sent to N., he would be glad to hear further from him, as he very much admires his style of satire, but can hardly approve of its biting causticity.

div.head: 679.—Tuesday, February 5, 1856.
div.p: N.——NO. Quite out of place.—T. S.

div.head: 680.—Friday, February 8, 1856.
div.p: A.H.—I am indeed pained and shocked, and can hardly believe it possible. WRITE all particulars to your broken-hearted father; also what has become of him, and who are cognizant of it.

div.head: 681.—Monday, February 18, 1856.
div.p: DE L’EAU CHAUDE.—39.

div.head: 682.—Tuesday, February 19, 1856.
div.p: CU. Y. TZ.—Votre associe est très inquiet; vos affaires s’arrangeront, mais vous ne devez pas vous absenter. Revenez ou écrire, à votre ami, compatriote de M. L.

div.head: 683.—Thursday, February 21, 1856.
div.p: LAVENDER.

div.head: 684.—Thursday, February 21, 1856.
div.p: HEALTH and HAPPINESS.—Guests numerous. Presents 40. Friends and pensioners received mementoes.—Excelsior.

div.head: 685.—Thursday, February 28, 1856.
div.p: LAVENDER.—Cannot answer Anonymous Letters.

div.head: 686.—Saturday, March 1, 1856.
div.p: DE L’EAU CHAUDE. Happy Returns.—39.

div.head: 687.—Saturday, March 1, 1856.
div.p: Z.—I return the question to G. C. Street, as before. The three relieving rounds received safely. Many thanks. Remember.

div.head: 688.—Friday, March 14, 1856.
div.p: ISABELL IS IN THE SAME Lodgings.

div.head: 689.—Tuesday, April 1, 1856.
div.p: HAMPSTEAD HEATH ENCLOSURE.—Look out! The Weasel is not asleep!

div.head: 690.—Wednesday, April 2, 1856.
div.p: TO M. R. B.—H.

div.head: 691.—Thursday, April 3, 1856.
div.p: HAMPSTEAD HEATH ENCLOSURE.—I am glad to hear Weasel is not asleep, as traps are laid for him.

div.head: 692.—Saturday, April 5, 15, 19, 1856.
div.p: THAT promised on the 7th and dated 10th January reached your brother only on the 17th March. His suspense was great, but faith steadfast. All are safe to the 10th January. By the time you see this there will be something awaiting you as before. Now safer than ever. Be vigilant, and look well within, for the meshes are weaving around you.—Sibella.

div.head: 693.—Wednesday, April 9, 1856.
div.p: EDWARD.—I am nearly mad. Suspense is death to me. My inquiries have only increased my sufferings. For God’s sake let me know the worst. Two wretched dreams have caused desolation that scarcely death could realize. Do WRITE.—St. Pancras.

div.head: 694.—Saturday, April 12, 1856.
div.p: L’INDISPOSITION de la “Séra du poête divin” est la seule chose au monde qui puisse me causer du vrai chagrin. Rassurez moi.—Votre puisque.

div.head: 695.—Thursday, May 1, 1856.
div.p: AUSTRALIA.—EMY. WRITE.—TOBY.

div.head: 696.—Wednesday, May 7, 1856.
div.p: SUSAN (not lovely dear).—£100, not more. Quick work.

div.head: 697.—Tuesday, May 13, 1856.
div.p: DRIVE it from you as you would a pestilence. WRITE immediately, or apply at Mr. W. P.’s.

div.head: 698.—Wednesday, May 14, 1856.
div.p: TO AMY.—7 first and last. Success is not to be desired, or sought for. E. . . . . . . r, the watchword through life.

div.head: 699.—Thursday, May 29, 1856.
div.p: M.D.—I will arrange as well as I can, and with great pleasure. In such a limited space I cannot describe all I feel, but I do feel deeply all I have read.

div.head: 700.—Friday, May 30, 1856.
div.p: TO E.—Ten Thousand THANKS.—Three magnificent ones have come to hand.—Your “Old Man.”

div.head: 701.—Tuesday, June 3, 4, 5, 1856.
div.p: TREU, fast, und verschwiegen. Haben sie mein so gar vergessen? Werde ich sie am sechsten abends sehen, wenn ich gehe? Wenn nicht, darf ich schreiben?

div.head: 702.—Wednesday, June 4, 1856.
div.p: BELLE MODELE, SERA, de 1854.—Je ne cherche que l’occasion de vous assurer que vous m’êtes plus chère que jamais. Si vous m’aimez, soignez cette précieuse santé. Notre séparation, les distractions du monde, ne font qu’augmenter mon attachement. Ecrivez dix mots de confiance.—12 Septembre—VOTRE PUISQUE.

div.head: 703.—Tuesday, June 10, 1856.
div.p: TREU, Fast, Verschwiegen.—Ich kann niemals vergessen. Das Schreiben wird aus Licht die Vergungen heiten aus ihrer Ruhe hervor zu klar zu helle bringen; aber wenn Sie es wünschen, so schreiben Sie, und Ich werde Ihnen auf Ihren Brief antworten.

div.head: 704.—Thursday, June 12, 1856.
div.p: UNALTERABLE, also, if you are my *. If you are, pray give me my own sign. You cannot mistake it. Then I shall not offend if I write. This very day let me have it.

div.head: 705.—Thursday, June 12, 1856.
div.p: FRIDAY, May 30.—I have the most beautiful horse in England, but not the most beautiful lady. Your silence pains me deeply. I cannot forget you.—M.

div.head: 706.—Friday, June 13, 1856.
div.p: UNALTERABLE.—Watch with O O O. Do WRITE immediately, as before. Not received, but mistake discovered, and deeply regretted.—Z.

div.head: 707.—Saturday, June 14, 1856.
div.p: TO A. B. C.—Have noticed the “Impression,” cherish the deepest gratitude, think (not certain) I know the good Samaritans. Pray be on the look out, above all look “upwards.” Remember what is at stake.—A. M. C.

div.head: 708.—Monday, June 16, 1856.
div.p: CHEF d’ŒUVRE du PEINTRE DIVIN.—La lettre que vous m’avez conjuré de détruire, sur laquelle j’avais inscrit ces mots, “Non e per me più felità,” c’est brulée. Celà m’a beaucoup coûté, puisqu’elle nous liait mystérieusement ensemble, mais je vous obéis. Ma vie m’est sans intérêt. Mon attachement augmente. Avez vous observé l’annonce antécédente?—PUISQUE.

div.head: 709.—Saturday, June 21, 1856.
div.p: HAMPSTEAD-HEATH ENCLOSURE.—Wake up, and PETITION PARLIAMENT.

div.head: 710.—Saturday, June 21, 1856.
div.p: PUISQUE.—I wish to be assured my letter is destroyed. ADDRESS me by my initials, Yes or No, certainly.

div.head: 711.—Saturday, June 21-25-28, 1856.
div.p: NOTHING of later date than 21st March received, consequently much anxiety. Your brother is returned. For you three, since that sent you on the 7th April.—Sibella. June 18.

div.head: 713.—Tuesday, June 24, 1856.
div.p: SOIR de CLAUDE LORRAINE.—Je suis convaincu qu’une annonce portant mon nom adopté, et avec référence à un sujet qui nous régardait, ne provenait pas de vous. Je l’attribue, donc, ou à quelque désir de me tendre une piége, ou à une coincidence incroyable, et presqu’ impossible.—Sempré il stesso.

div.head: 714.—Tuesday, June 24, 1856.
div.p: MANCHESTER.—Only just before your letter reached my hotel in London I obtained fresh light from the public documents upon the great question in which we are both engaged. Prices do not fluctuate much (especially cotton), because the annexation question (which chiefly affects us), though complicated (look at Marcy’s note), may probably be finished, if a proper mediator can be found. And why not? Answer this. It is understood on both sides that the independence of the Parent State is to be maintained; and, if necessary, vindicated, notwithstanding internal cabal and unwarranted external intrigue and interference, which latter is, after all, the chief cause of the misunderstanding between the Powers. Your ’cuteness, I see, distances pretty considerably my slowness, distracted as I am with the States’ affairs; but Weasel is not caught twice in the same trap. Address as before.

div.head: 715.—Tuesday, June 24, 1856.
div.p: PUISQUE.—A reply so headed in this morning’s paper is not mine. I have not replied at all until now, and shall not do so again in this manner. Some mistake, or curiosity, or worse perhaps. WRITE to me, name in full, post-office, giving an address: I will reply, giving you one, then there can be no more mistakes. Do this at once. Grief and anxiety are rapidly doing their work. My idol is indeed a rare combination of tenderness, talent, and every virtue. Love and admiration still contend, represented now by two sweet cherubs.—Ever YOUR OWN; June 21, 1856.

div.head: 716.—Saturday, June 28, 1856.
div.p: TOM came ashore yesterday, in the bark Hope, and wrote directly. He is a shy, odd fellow, rather slow, but thoroughly honest, very like Parson Adams.—June 27, 1856.

div.head: 717.—Thursday, July 3, 1856.
div.p: TOM put out last week in a storm, but, as the glass is rising, hopes to find his way home soon, though he is alone in his slow boat, without a pilot.—July 2, 1856.

div.head: 718.—Thursday, July 3, 1856.
div.p: FEUILLE de HETRE.—Je suis désolé d’apprendre, que vous avez été souffrante, et je suis en proie à des anxiétés cruelles puisque vous avez tant à entreprendre. Vous perdre serait mon coup de mort. Que le Ciel vous protège. Ces lignes n’étaient que trop dévorés. Le tableau ne vous est plus rival.—Il triste é povero asilo.

div.head: 719.—Monday, July 7, 1856.
div.p: NICHT EINE MILLION.

div.head: 720.—Tuesday, July 8, 1856.
div.p: KEINE MILLION, gar nichts, ist erwartet.

div.head: 721.—Wednesday, July 9, 1856.
div.p: MONEYMARSH.—SINGLE.

div.head: 722.—Thursday, July 10, 1856.
div.p: GENUG FUR ALLES.

div.head: 723.—Monday, July 14, 1856.
div.p: GWENLLIAN.—Tuesday or Wednesday.

div.head: 724.—Monday, July 14, 1856.
div.p: YOU promised to let me know your wishes and views of the matter in full. You have not done so. I feel that I am unkindly treated. You think it right to keep me always in the dark, and consider one unworthy your confidence. London, 12th.

div.head: 725.—Monday, July 14, 1856.
div.p: MANCHESTER.—E.—Recent public documents have supplied me with the most satisfactory intelligence upon the annexation question. Dallas is to fix everything. But you must know that before I write again direct, I have to satisfy myself as to the views of the parent state, which I conclude to be all along pacific, though I am not cute in negotiation, having been so long a squatter on the sunny banks of the far west. I am particularly gratified to find that you cordially agree with me upon this question.—Crampton has reached this.—V. M. F.—July 12.

div.head: 726.—Saturday, July 19, 1856.
div.p: MY COLOURS are NAILED, not tied to the MASTHEAD.—T.

div.head: 727.—Tuesday, July 22, 1856.
div.p: X.Y. Z.—In answer to yours of the 9th inst., Tom writes that his sisters misunderstand him—they living in society, he in retirement, never giving, and therefore too slowly taking a hint. How can he help feeling towards them sincere brotherly love, when he is so fully aware of their many valuable qualities, including an affectionate disposition, good sense, superior education, and accomplishments? I tell him to try and join them in a holiday trip before the winter.—Y. A. F.

div.head: 728.—Tuesday, July 22, 1856.
div.p: GROSSE FREUDE!—Aber warum hast du zweifel gehabt?—T.

div.head: 729.—Wednesday, July 23, 1856.
div.p: HEUTE in GEFANGNISS; morgen frei.—July 22.

div.head: 730.—Thursday, July 24, 1856.
div.p: MANCHESTER, E.—The discordance of my private despatches with the public documents suddenly and most unexpectedly arrests my progress. In retiring to the old Prairie settlement, I grieve to find myself obliged to record what you, I know, fully believe, the entire sincerity and disinterestedness of my long and anxious endeavours to arrange this question.—YOURS.—July 23, 1856.

div.head: 731.—Friday, July 25, 1856.
div.p: FAIRS.—Middlesex to wit.—These annual gatherings cannot be postponed, for a good deal of business is done by help of the gilt gingerbread, toys, and pan-pipes. The scaffolding for the shows at the last two broke down about three weeks ago, and could not be mended in time.

div.head: 732.—Saturday, July 26, 1856.
div.p: MISTIFIED, not Gratified, but Pacified. My colours have been rather roughly torn away; but I am trying to steady myself by keeping a sharp look out upon the windmills, and nailing an old head of Don Quixote at the prow.—Tom.

div.head: 733.—Monday, July 28, 1856.
div.p: MANCHESTER, E.—My favourite clipper does not sail yet; so it is just possible that I may get some private news, which, you must see, is quite indispensable to support the public documents.—YOURS.—July 26, 1856.

div.head: 734.—Thursday, July 31, 1856.
div.p: IMMER der Deinige, aber der zweifel erscheint in der Ferne.

div.head: 735.—Thursday, July 31, 1856.
div.p: FEUILLE de HETRE to ——.—Your friend B. will soon call upon you, as of old. He will not allude to the subject, and pray be careful that you do not. Tell me if you understand. Why may I not write?

div.head: 736.—Thursday, July 31, 1856.
div.p: MANCHESTER, E.—I am still without any private news to support the public documents. You know that I cannot act upon these. The Britishers withhold all confidence from the straightforward, singlestick settler. However, I shall not cross the water yet, being determined to spare no reasonable efforts to settle successfully the question which has so long and anxiously occupied my attention.—Yours, July 30, 1856.

div.head: 737.—Friday, August 1, 1856.
div.p: AVOW.—1855, December 5th.—J. N09014.

div.head: 738.—Friday, August 1, 1856.
div.p: DER ZWEIFEL VERSCHWINDET.

div.head: 739.—Friday, August 1, 1856.
div.p: Z.Y. X., E.—The news you sent me from the opposite shore is most gratifying and important. You must allow for my imperfect instructions in the foreign tongue; but I believe I understand your intentions now, and, of course, I shall follow them exactly. I wish I knew our mutual friend’s hotel, for I feel that I ought to anticipate his visit. What can your last inquiry mean?—Yours ever. T.

div.head: 741.—Saturday, August 2, 1856.
div.p: EMILIE, on the 22nd, sent No. 3, to Rmgviozx; on the 28th, No. 4 to the city, directed to our friend there. Have they your address? Give me full directions. Why not poste-restante as before?—July 30.

div.head: 742.—Saturday, August 9, 1856.
