div.p: FAITH.—The last news eminently satisfactory. The change spoken of accords fully with the expectations formed. Rest assured that all is as well as possible, arrangements are perfected, and every contingency prepared for. Away and returned. Address as usual. It is mine. Ever.

div.head: 1059.—Saturday, September 3, 1859.
div.p: TO G.—“Take each man’s censure, but reserve thy judgment.”—2 Cor., IV. c., 9 v. T. “write” home.

div.head: 1060.—Monday, September 5, 1859.
div.p: OUR PEOPLE RETURN September 7.

div.head: 1061.—Tuesday, September 6, 1859.
div.p: T.W. S.—Il me faut un cœur où je puisse répandre ma peine. Ecris-moi. À toi à jamais, O. W. D.

div.head: 1062.—Friday, September 9, 1859.
div.p: TO the HEART of STONE.—Why torture the victim longer? Bright prospects shine if you meet on the instant. He has been ruined over and over in screening you. It is the last attempt. If you oppose him now, a few days will put it out of his power to do all he desires for you—this is more than can be told. He forgives from his heart, and will never allude to the past. If he has offended, he hopes, alas, to be forgiven. Let him see the child and kiss it. The nurse shall bear the note fixing time and place. Let it be where you now are.

div.head: 1063.—Saturday, September 10, 1859.
div.p: TO EPSOM.—You are not truly spoken of. When I see you, I will consult with you as to the best way to set matters right. Molehills have been made mountains. I have so much confidence in you I shall never speak or think of the past. Poison against you has been industriously strewed in my path. Forgive. Watch for me at noon. Continue in sight, then I will advance, not otherwise. I know myself too well to intrude. All as you will.

div.head: 1064.—Monday, September 12, 1859.
div.p: EXCELSIOR.

div.head: 1065.—Thursday, September 15, 1859.
div.p: EPSOM.—“The Times,” 13th and 14th September instant. On the 13th three—on the 14th two. This is the 19th since——. You can write—I cannot. Your writing will show sincerity, and that the communication was your own.

div.head: 1066.—Thursday, September 15, 1859.
div.p: EPSOM AGAIN.—I hope you are not labouring under the impression that, by advising as I did, I am changed.—God forbid! Was “My dearest Friend” yours, or is it a mere coincidence? I hope your h——’s fears are groundless.

div.head: 1067.—Saturday, September 17, 1859.
div.p: MYSTERY.—Present conduct very suspicious to him who knows all. It indicates, also, desire to delude, and exhibits all the past professions to have been for some purpose. Meet as ordinary friends where you now are, or never in this world. No more “delusion.” No more notes such as “I have been much annoyed,” &c. The Martyr can no longer endure such ungenerous petty insult. It out-Herods all. You shall have justice done you so far as unfounded reports go, but the spirits of departed parents and some respect for self as a man demand that I no longer rest under the false accusations of the ——. Farewell.

div.head: 1068.—Thursday, September 22, 1859.
div.p: TWENTY-FIVE.—Près de toi c’est la vie, loin de toi c’est mourir. Attendre et espérer je t’en conjure.

div.head: 1069.—Thursday, September 29, 1859.
div.p: WALES.—“RETURN or WRITE immediately.” This done over and over, but all rejected. “All parties immovable.” These absurd words make me doubt “sincerity.” “Very nervous.” Why so? I will never allude to the past, nor think of it. I forgive all, whatever may have been. Ever study wishes. Sent for letters in real name. Never yet a line. Fear not threats. No future tales, whether true or groundless, will annoy me. Your father and mother are better.

div.head: 1070.—Friday, September 30, 1859.
div.p: ROMANS XII. 9.

div.head: 1071.—Monday, October 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 1859.
div.p: TO — ——.—Can’t you recognize a quotation from your own letter? I often think “of that pretty but affecting tale of,” &c. No, not to the last address, but the previous one.

div.head: 1072.—Monday, October 3, 1859.
div.p: V.—Près de toi c’est la vie, loin de toi c’est mourir. Most strange to read one’s own inmost thought and yearning thus syllabled forth by another, like a dream told back to the dreamer! Daily and hourly I repeat to myself those words: but alas! for me, la vie court vite, c’est la mort qui dure, et j’attends sans espérer.—J.

div.head: 1073.—Saturday, October 8, 1859.
div.p: K—— POTT. Sploce. Lak. The Mutability!

div.head: 1074.—Friday, October 28, 31, 1859.
div.p: MARIA.—Dear Wife. I am well. “Good night.” “All’s well.”—EDWARD.

div.head: 1075.—Friday, November 4, 1859.
div.p: MARIA.—That is done; give me a name, and I will write to the old address. “Good night; all’s well.”—EDWARD.

div.head: 1076.—Monday, November 7, 1859.
div.p: MARIA.—It is done. Give me a name. I will write to the old address. I am well, dearest. “Good night, all’s well. Ever yours, EDWARD.

div.head: 1077.—Tuesday, November 8, 1859.
div.p: HAND OBLIVISCENDUM.—Acknowledged £20.—4th Nov., 1859.

div.head: 1078.—Friday, November 11, 1859.
div.p: MARIA.—You have done most wisely. Always do the same. “Good night, all’s well.” Yours ever, EDWARD.

div.head: 1079.—Monday, November 21, 1859.
div.p: MARY.—Is it safe to write to you, and to direct as I did the last? “Good night, all’s well.” Your ever affectionate Husband.

div.head: 1080.—Monday, November 28, 1859.
div.p: LIVERPOOL.—Why not? ill, not Monday. Write.

div.head: 1081.—Friday, December 2, 1859.
div.p: FAITH.—The acquaintance is of the slightest, and conversation on such matters is out of the question. The difficulties and evils are fully understood. Does the P. S. concern the affair named some time back? Only five. Ever.

div.head: 1082.—Monday, December 12, 1859.
div.p: AUSTRALIA: Emy: Write: Toby.

div.head: 1083.—Saturday, December 31, 1859.
div.p: TO “I AM GOING HOME.”—Give me your address. Confidence is felt. You have not been avoided. Our business is settled at your pleasure. All orphan’s difficulties can be dispelled if true friends rally round and help with kind encouragement and explanation.—Dec. 30, 1859.

div.head: 1084.—Monday, January 5, 1860.
div.p: J.K.—Alas, no improvement since last year. I am still lingering on the brink of the precipice, notwithstanding “Stick no Bills” and all the kind advice which was then given. A happy new year to you.—MARIANNE.

div.head: 1085.—Thursday, January 26, 1860.
div.p: TOP of the HILL.—14.—Thank God! Wish to take leave of that growing 14. It may turn saucy. But Patience shall be a duty.

div.head: 1086.—Tuesday, January 31, 1860.
div.p: EXOTIC.—This is final. I have suffered greatly, yet admire your fidelity and strength of character. May you never repent it. Good-bye, God bless you.—FRANK Dody.

div.head: 1087.—Wednesday, February 1, 1860.
div.p: ROSE LEAVES.

div.head: 1088.—Friday, February 3, 1860.
div.p: FAITH.—Ninety-nine instead of one hundred and fifty-two. A LETTER AWAITS you as before. Ever.

div.head: 1089.—Friday, February 10, 1860.
div.p: EMERGENT.—F. D.

div.head: 1090.—Tuesday, February 14, 1860.
div.p: TO the INNOCENT.—Yes, on the instant. It cannot be after. Your manner and ways, coupled with the truly absurd stories of the past, have made you appear (to those not knowing you) other than you are. Would that all the world was as amiable, virtuous, and good. Your FRIEND.

div.head: 1091.—Tuesday, February 28, 1860.
div.p: THE Lark they may prison, but her SPIRIT is risen, and soars to its own native Skies.—WRITE, in strict confidence, to Reciprocal, care of X. Y., 58, York-street, Dublin.

div.head: 1092.—Friday, March 2, 1860.
div.p: TOP OF THE HILL.—14th Anniversary.—I saw it. She suffers real want. She must make another effort to move. The most trifling help is valuable in such distress. She says that patience, faith, resignation, are sacred duties.

div.head: 1093.—Wednesday, March 7, 1860.
div.p: GLEN.—SPECKLED FOWLS, buya—buy my mackerel!

div.head: 1094.—Thursday, March 15, 1860.
div.p: RENT.—RECEIVED YOURS; have long left town for my musical duties, the salary for which hardly permits constant advertising; therefore you must contrive how I can write to you. Your advice and convictions are equally excellent; still the days of “manna” descending have ceased. Remember advice regarding your health. Mr. Expert, ever your own fondly and eternally, Sophy.

div.head: 1095.—Saturday, March 17, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 1860.
div.p: REFLECT!—Remember, I live still. Has been joyfully received. Where can I meet you or write? God bless you.

div.head: 1096.—Saturday, April 21, 1860.
div.p: E. V. E. R. Y.—Not punishable.

div.head: 1097.—Wednesday, May 2, 1860.
div.p: NELLA bruna la costanza!

div.head: 1098.—Friday, May 18, 1860.
div.p: NINTH.—Would it be safe to do so? Great caution requisite.—Y——.

div.head: 1099.—Saturday, May 19, 1860.
div.p: WASHINGTON FRIEND APPROACHES LONDON.

div.head: 1100.—Thursday, May 24, 1860.
div.p: A.and E.—You do me an injustice to say that I am tampering with you. Your kind notes were duly acknowledged. The first was destroyed “unopened” (?). The second was returned. Though I may never have the happiness of seeing you again the memory of the past will supply the tide-flow of joy. Farewell.

div.head: 1101.—Friday, May 25, 1860.
div.p: PAIR the ARABIC NUMERALS; placing their like tens, for the Districts; in the same line; and their like units, for the Guilds; in the same column. By this chessboard arrangement, the hundred pairs will be sections of a Phalanx, common to both.—T. F.

div.head: 1102.—Saturday, May 26, 1860.
div.p: A.and E.—You do me an injustice to say I am tampering with you. Your kind notes were duly acknowledged. The first was destroyed “unopened.” The other was returned. Vide the Times, May 24. N.B. These vowels “A. E.” may be adopted by a third rival party for the purpose of misleading through falsehood, but the true vowels “U. and I.” being relatives, will not be deceived by capital letters or capital hoaxers. The wise accept only as true evidence hand-writing, signature, and seal.

div.head: 1103.—Tuesday, June 5, 1860.
div.p: N.D.—Could not succeed on ——. You know ——. Hope better fortune.—WRITE.

div.head: 1104.—Friday, July 20, 1860.
div.p: ELIZABETH STREET and every one. READ this COLUMN of yesterday.—F. M. S.

div.head: 1105.—Tuesday, July 31, 1860.
div.p: Αινιγμα.—How, without money, you can get steamers; and as many more steamers you get, as more money you can possess?—X. to B. S.

div.head: 1106.—Thursday, August 2, 1860.
div.p: YOUR INITIALS in Hair.—J——. July 31.

div.head: 1107.—Wednesday, August 22, 1860.
div.p: HEW.—M. at S., much better. I have done very well. Made 65 this week. Seconds for about 2,000. Hear again in two months.

div.head: 1108.—Saturday, September 1, 3, 1860.
div.p: ANTONIA.—Circumstances which appear adverse sometimes prove favourable, and the faith I hold will not permit me to lose hope. Yours truly, Annie.

div.head: 1109.—Tuesday, September 4, 1860.
div.p: THANKS.—I am, since Tuesday, in the W. C. B. H., and I shall, probably, remain until you tell me to leave. I have been everywhere. One little garden is the only one well looked after.

div.head: 1110.—Saturday, September 22, 1860.
div.p: ANNIE.—The excursion may not now extend to Geneva or Paris. Yours faithfully, Antonia.

div.head: 1111.—Monday, September 24, 1860.
div.p: ADELINE.—Your happiness must be considered.

div.head: 1112.—Thursday, September 27, 1860.
div.p: J.A. W.—I cannot. Yes, I do very much. Thursday or Friday, at 4, at old place.

div.head: 1113.—Thursday, September 27, 1860.
div.p: HORRID CREATURE.—Keep up your courage, and trust in God; He knows your innocence, and will protect you. All your friends will be faithful till death. Patience. Subteakhoojiaca.

div.head: 1114.—Friday, September 28, 1860.
div.p: X.Y. Z.—8 o’clock.—Portugal.

div.head: 1115.—Monday, October 1, 1860.
div.p: ALE VRAI CROIX.—I could not send before; fear I cannot again, but ever believe I am “Fidèle à Mort.” Did you receive the picture?

div.head: 1116.—Tuesday, October 2, 1860.
div.p: TOIFEY, Toifey.—No letter as promised. Assert your rights. No white slave. Write. I go S. W. on Wednesday, October 3—return to town on Monday, October 22. Meet me that day. God bless you. Thine now as ever. Despair. When the heart heaves. Return.

div.head: 1117.—Tuesday, October 2, 1860.
div.p: M.H. (Omega).—From justice and friendship you owe me some explanations respecting the calumnies emanating from Newcastle, in order that I may be enabled to defend myself in future against similar aspersions, though (as a Christian) I may not be allowed to retaliate. Your letter shall be answered immediately.—Kappa.

div.head: 1118.—Monday, October 8, 1860.
div.p: MAIBLUMCHEN, warum hast du nicht geschrieben? Es verlangt mich zehr deinen zustanden zu wissen. Kanust du, mich au dem acht und zwanrigsten. Monatstage zu treffen, mit mir verabreden?

div.head: 1119.—Wednesday, October 10, 1860.
div.p: TO M. A. A.—Ich habe gelebt und geliebt. Farewell?

div.head: 1120.—Thursday, October 11, 1860.
div.p: ISABEL.

div.head: 1121.—Monday, October 15, 16, 1860.
div.p: DEAREST BEIDES.—VISIT the BLACKMOOR at once, and all will be arranged, and write to London Club. Mother very ill.

div.head: 1122.—Tuesday, October 16, 1860.
div.p: E——N.—I learn from Mrs. L., that you are the victim of a foul conspiracy and gross delusions. I have ever been, am now, and mean under any circumstances to continue, unchanged and faithful to 9th Nov., 1860. Therefore the vacancy will not and cannot be filled up as you suppose. Think of this in your moments of remorse. I found no letter with yours. I shall not try to find or molest you; but let me write you more fully. I wish you to be happy.—GRUNTLE.

div.head: 1123.—Wednesday, October 17, 1860.
div.p: BEIDES.—“Have a care.” You are near destruction, but still have friends. Go to the Blackmoor at once, and a kind arrangement will be effected.—E——

div.head: 1124.—Friday, October 19, 1860.
div.p: B.T.—You must come—it is your duty. G—— says so seriously. Extremes all but meet.

div.head: 1125.—Monday, October 22, 1860.
div.p: CORRESPONDANCE.—Adressez-vous par billet au bureau convenu. Vous y trouverez plusieurs Lancaster. Le bureau est ouvert depuis 10 jusqu’a 3. Tout va bien.

div.head: 1126.—Tuesday, October 23, 25, 1860.
div.p: ADRESSEZ-VOUS, Great Winchester-street, city, vous en trouverez 5 au nom convenu, le bureau est au rez-de-chaussée à gauche. Soyez tranquille tout va bien.—Pervi, Luxembourg, 11.

div.head: 1127.—Thursday, October 25, 1860.
div.p: P.A. C. hopes now for mutual sympathy—time and thoughts work wonders. A reply is asked, though hardly hoped for, saying that certain reports (so quickly spread abroad after I left) might one day turn out truths. The 25th prox. Ever yours.

div.head: 1128.—Monday, October 29, 1860.
div.p: ALPHA.—Does this vexation proceed from you or from his enemies who employed similar means last May and June? If from you, you will please to cease, or you may see him a few days hence a wanderer, once more, by your fault. Though you imagine him changeable, God will strengthen him not to swerve from the path of honour and conscience respecting M. Z.—Kappa.

div.head: 1129.—Thursday, November 8, 1860.
div.p: R.E.—Tuesday, the 13th. Very great.

div.head: 1130.—Wednesday, November 14, 1860.
div.p: QUEEN of BUSHIRE.—Remember Ali Bux. WRITE at once. You know where.

div.head: 1131.—Tuesday, November 20, 1860.
div.p: HANG OUT the BANNERS.—COMMUNICATE all at once, if not too late. All may be arranged. T. L. and T. A.

div.head: 1132.—Monday, November 26, 1860.
div.p: P.A. C. hopes that silence gives consent. Time and circumstance are the keys to real sentiments. One word is asked in reciprocity, and anxiously waited for. The 25th prox. Ever yours.

div.head: 1133.—Tuesday, November 27, 1860.
div.p: J.G.—Oui. Depuis le neuf. Parole. Violettes arrivées mille remercimens. Souffrant et très occupé. Je t’embrasse.

div.head: 1134.—Saturday, December 1, 1860.
div.p: J.—RECEIVED ALL. Not before twenty-second. Will call. Doctor satisfied. Trash. H. Read Hermine. Await opportunity to write.

div.head: 1135.—Thursday, December 6, 1860.
div.p: T.G.—Arrived all right, as arranged; M. O. D. W. Lovely country, but no good cigars. I wish you could bring some. Pray write soon to Y. O. D. H.—A. E. T.

div.head: 1136.—Tuesday, December 11, 12, 1860.
div.p: NENNEN Sie den Tag und den Platz: wenn Sie mich nicht sehen können in Ihren Amt?

div.head: 1137.—Saturday, December 15, 1860.
div.p: DIDO.—All will be right if done at once.—WIDO WEE.

div.head: 1138.—Saturday, December 29, 1860.
div.p: L’AMI FENTON’S est parti le lundi seulement, je reste en ville. Je t’embrasse.

div.head: 1139.—Tuesday, January 1, 1861.
div.p: T.G.—D. L. landed at Palermo, went through Sicily to Messina, up to Naples and Capua; and now, with heart true to the cause, waits events at F. Viva Italia! Quite well. Nothing new. How is D. W. all this time? Y. O. D. H.—A. E. T.

div.head: 1140.—Thursday, January 10, 1861.
div.p: JD. . LC. . Well × J. H. D. . name in full length. High-street, Dorkg, Surrey.

div.head: 1141.—Saturday, January 19, 1861.
div.p: QUEEN of BUSHIRE.—Care not for the Dragon. Poor Ali Bux still waits for the waggon, at the old address.

div.head: 1142.—Tuesday, January 29, 1861.
div.p: WHAT you wish is done.—W—— No——.

div.head: 1143.—Friday, February 1, 1861.
div.p: ORION’S BOAT.—Renew, and make an end.

div.head: 1144.—Saturday, February 2, 1861.
div.p: SCROOGE has promised. Write to W.

div.head: 1145.—Saturday, February 2, 4, 1861.
div.p: TO QUOD TIBI ID ALII.—“Pray, dearest S., write.” Veto X., to Tavistock, London.

div.head: 1146.—Saturday, February 2, 1861.
div.p: T.G.—RETURN to Z., on the day appointed, M. O. D. W. You know when and where, and that I am Y. S. H.—A. E. T.

div.head: 1147.—Saturday, February 2, 1861.
div.p: Αναγη.—I cannot thank you enough for keeping your promise. F. S. and leaving in C., venture to B., completing their service. There is no personal news, except that, through delay in receipt of letter from consulate, I am unable to return and enter de T. How little you know of that morning’s history—the intense effort required not to involve some one very dear—it would have been ruinous; and yet how much I would risk if necessary—I do not, I shall not, forget. Reconsider what are circumstances to a will like yours! Pray WRITE, if only once more.—Yours ever, T.

div.head: 1148.—Wednesday, February 6, 1861.
div.p: NEVER.

div.head: 1149.—Wednesday, February 6, 1861.
div.p: ADIEU. God bless you! Farewell.

div.head: 1150.—Saturday, February 9, 1861.
div.p: T.D.—L. C. well. T. H. D., name in full length.—High-street, Dorking, Surrey.

div.head: 1151.—Saturday, February 9, 1861.
div.p: THE TIMES, May 9, 1859.—“Hope, ever hope.” I have and will always do so; yet I have had no intelligence of you since May 24, ’59. Can you not let me hear from you, directly or indirectly? I trust that when Spring returns (the flower it blooms) that friends so sincere will meet again.

div.head: 1152.—Friday, February 15, 1861.
div.p: E.to B—— O.—The cough is well. I wish to see you. What we arranged. They would not pub Lupus.

div.head: 1153.—Saturday, February 16, 1861.
div.p: HOPE, ever hope. I have, and will always do so; yet I have had no intelligence of you since May 24, 1859. Will you let me know how you can hear from me, as I do not know your address? You can have mine from Mrs. Turner, 26, Brewer-street, Pimlico; then friends so sincere will meet again.

div.head: 1154.—Thursday, February 21, 1861.
div.p: LOOK HERE—remember next Tuesday.

div.head: 1155.—Thursday, February 21, 1861.
div.p: X.Y. Z.—Yes. Good news this morning. I did not advertise on Tuesday.

div.head: 1156.—Friday, February 22, 1861.
div.p: TODD oder TODT? Schreibe—welcher, dem “Carbonari.”—Exchange, Dundee.

div.head: 1157.—Thursday, February 28, 1861.
div.p: JACK has LOST VICTORIA TRAIN. Wishes to explain to F. this delay. Fix a time.

div.head: 1158.—Thursday, February 28, 1861.
div.p: FIFTEEN POUNDS RETRIBUTION RECEIVED, S. S. Matt. vi. 15. When? where? and, if myself personally or others of the family who have been wronged? Initials, and I’ll seek no more. Address, General P. O., Clapham.

div.head: 1159.—Friday, March 1, April 1, 1861.
div.p: Αναγη.—I cannot thank you enough for keeping your promise. F. S. and leaving in C., return to B., completing their service. There is no personal news, except that, through delay in receipt of letter from consulate, I am unable to return and enter de T. How little you know of that morning’s history—the intense effort required not to involve some one very dear—it would have been ruinous; and yet how much I would risk if necessary—I do not, shall not forget. Reconsider what are circumstances to a will like yours! Pray WRITE, if only once more. January 15.—I have just seen an obituary notice—how sad, sudden, unexpected! How much I wish I could be of some service to you!—Your ever, T.

div.head: 1160.—Friday, March 15, 1861.
div.p: A.B. C.—This is the first time. The value and importance of the matters in question are overestimated, but act justly. The name (three words) appears several times.

div.head: 1161.—Thursday, March 28, 1861.
div.p: STOOPUMS.—Shall be in town on Friday, leave on Sunday. WRITE to old lodgings what time “Pomp” on Saturday must see you. IDIOT.

div.head: 1162.—Friday, March 29, 1861.
div.p: STOOPUMS.—There is a letter at old place. Send for it. Forgot this yesterday. IDIOT.

div.head: 1163.—Monday, April 1, 1861.
div.p: HAMPSTEAD HEATH ENCLOSURE.—Something’s up!

div.head: 1164.—Wednesday, April 3, 1861.
div.p: ORION’S BOAT.—Come with all papers (H. C.) Missing memorandum of E. & G., former year, found.

div.head: 1165.—Thursday, April 4, 1861.
div.p: TO VIOLET.—Keep up your heart. Trust in me. I have seen your Friend, and will do all for the best. You are, and always will be, my first thought. I have now received three letters from you, viz.;—13th February, 1st and 28th March: and have done all you wished. No. 2.

div.head: 1166.—Monday, April 8, 1861.
div.p: JOLLY to RUMMY.—Please give me a right understanding, as I am in a fix, and I will answer you in return.

div.head: 1167.—Monday, April 22, 1861.
div.p: ALL RIGHT, my own darling E.—April 16.

div.head: 1168.—Wednesday, May 1, 1861.
div.p: ORION’S BOAT.—No writing. I will see you.

div.head: 1169.—Wednesday, May 1, 1861.
div.p: TO the ONE WHO CAN UNDERSTAND.—You cannot, I am sure, now fail in your promise voluntarily given. I pray you to let this painful suspense end, and accounts come as before. R. has returned to remain. Let this appeal be sufficient.

div.head: 1170.—Wednesday, May 8, 1861.
div.p: TOM CAT.—A Boy on the 2nd May, in Paris.—Pray write to B., who is now free! He waits to tell you all. Direct under cover to J. R. S. You may safely write.

div.head: 1171.—Thursday, May 9, 1861.
div.p: BEAULIEU.—Received.—Ps. xx., 3, 4.

div.head: 1172.—Wednesday, May 22, 1861.
div.p: TOM CAT.—Another letter has been SENT to Bruxelles, poste restante. An interview in pure and sincere friendship is all that is asked, at any time and place you may name. Do not delay, it is of vital importance to me, and much so to you. Depend upon your own wishes being carried out.—B.

div.head: 1173.—Monday, May 27, 1861.
div.p: ORION’S BOAT.—Wait for me. E. Y. 2. You mistook.

div.head: 1174.—Tuesday, May 28, 1861.
div.p: R.S. P., Water Colourer.

div.head: 1175.—Saturday, June 1, 1861.
div.p: AFAINT HEART NEVER WINS a FAIR LADY. The ANONYMOUS CORRESPONDENT whose letter was posted in Lombard Street, on Thursday last, is requested to be MORE EXPLICIT. R. sticks to his craft, and will persevere when he sees his way. Address, Post-office, Vigo-street, Regent-street.

div.head: 1176.—Tuesday, June 11, 1861.
div.p: BRIDGEWATER.—I am horrified at what I have discovered. If possible let me know the worst.

div.head: 1177.—Tuesday, June 18, 19, 1861.
div.p: HONEYCOMB.—Please “journey” home end next week. WRITE immediately, sending address. You have not been kind to IDIOT.

div.head: 1178.—Tuesday, June 18, 1861.
div.p: FELIX.—138 and special, right. T. leaves home July 3. Congratulate Ce. on late successful performance. Proposed plan approved, but come sooner if possible. Remember us to Scrup & Co. All well, and unite in regards. Addio.

div.head: 1179.—Thursday, June 20, 1861.
div.p: SMUDE.—Sah nettirw eciwt. Syats ta sih ecffio rof eht tneserp.—June 19.

div.head: 1180.—Friday, June 21, 24, 26, 1861.
div.p: PORTMANTEAU to PACK. I still dream.

div.head: 1181.—Thursday, June 27, 1861.
div.p: A.B. Z. si yltsenrae detseuqer ot etacinummoc tuohtiw yaled. Ma ni yrev taerg elbuort. Dna eriuqer etaidemmi ecivda.—53, Reppu Ruomyes-teerts, Namtrop-erauqs.

div.head: 1182.—Monday, July 1, 2, 1861.
div.p: CHAPEL of EASE.—NELLY.—He is delirious. He wishes to hear from you. We fear the worst. You know the address. His friends have inserted this. A line from you may save him yet.

div.head: 1183.—Friday, July 12, 1861.
div.p: SMUDE.—Eht tsop eciffo ta Hgiel si dehctaw. Lotsirb lliw od. Ekat erac.—July 11.

div.head: 1184.—Friday, July 19, 1861.
div.p: J.B. and S. S. are quits.

div.head: 1185.—Tuesday, July 30, 1861.
div.p: W.H. D. Elsie. C. C. C. You are mistaken. This is my testimony. Yours, as ever, for ever. Robert.

div.head: 1186.—Thursday, August 8, 9, 1861.
div.p: X.Y. Z.—August 12. 8 o’clock.—PORTUGAL.

div.head: 1187.—Thursday, August 8, 1861.
div.p: GIOIA MIA.—Pipey and Beauty quite well. Cases paid for. Sorry to disappoint you, but too uncertain. Letter by first opportunity. Thank J., to whom I could write? A toi corps et âme.

div.head: 1188.—Wednesday, August 14, 1861.
div.p: TOM MOORE, No. 1. RECEIVED yours. You write, I will do as you propose.

div.head: 1189.—Wednesday, August 21, 1861.
div.p: TOM MOORE.—I shall not leave London unless with you. Your letters give hopes (No. 2).

div.head: 1190.—Thursday, August 22, 1861.
div.p: STELLA.—Aan, Bala, Na Bud, Ke Ay, Bala, Bud. There is a LETTER for you.—C. Y.—35, Post-office, G——W.

div.head: 1191.—Saturday, August 31, 1861.
div.p: TOM MOORE.—YOURS RECEIVED. Thanks. How is T.’s health? Polly’s visit was a great kindness, and it has allayed a very anxious feeling. B. is a bachelor (No. 3).

div.head: 1192.—Tuesday, September 3, 1861.
div.p: TOM MOORE.—B. will be there (4).

div.head: 1193.—Tuesday, September 3, 1861.
div.p: BLUE ENAMEL CROSS.—I cannot trust W. Letter received. I accept all its terms. Mine until death. Be patient.

div.head: 1194.—Wednesday, September 4, 1861.
div.p: L’ESCORT RECEIVED YOURS. However well himself complains of the conduct of your protégée. He gives him great trouble, and unless you could give hope for an early “Duncaster” meeting he fears the necessity of applying for help to Dr. Evans. Having no project he shall not leave S. before the 15th September.—Scarborough, Sept. 1.

div.head: 1195.—Friday, September 6, 1861.
div.p: LORELEI.—The Anthropophagous didn’t gobble the partridges.

div.head: 1196.—Tuesday, September 10, 1861.
div.p: S.to L., the 8 R’s, and W.—CHARLES URQUHARDT NEWPORT TINLEY has not suffered from the eels.

div.head: 1197.—Saturday, September 14, 1861.
div.p: TOM MOORE—Yours received. Six months is quite right. I think B. had better see you next week; but if you think otherwise, a small parcel, containing the writing, shall be left at the Rail, you to call for it as you pass (5).

div.head: 1198.—Tuesday, September 17, 20, 24, 1861.
div.p: N.W.—L’Amaro è Molto. Helurchen.

div.head: 1199.—Tuesday, September 17, 1861.
div.p: TOM MOORE.—B. travels upon the second day named, unless you advise differently by post. B. can arrange the day to your advice (6).

div.head: 1200.—Thursday, September 19, 1861.
div.p: WILL you GIVE me a BOA at Brighton. Norwood Junction, 10.30 P.M. Shall we never meet again? The word to Nina, Post-office, Norwood. S. marked “M. T.” may reach and console the stranger.

div.head: 1201.—Tuesday, September 24, 1861.
div.p: C.C. C. I must see you. This place is not what I expected (Plants). I have a rival (foreign) earning double as much as I do. You heard what happened to my money and papers in the city. E. W., B’ps Std., Herts.—X.

div.head: 1202.—Wednesday, September 25, 1861.
div.p: TOM MOORE.—INSTRUCTIONS will be WAITING you at the Railway Station, the Parcel office, when this meets your eye. Still hoping (7).

div.head: 1203.—Thursday, September 26, 1861.
div.p: TOM MOORE.—You are favoured in your powers, so do persist and persevere, but judiciously, and the difficulty, we hope, will then yield, though at a late moment. Most seriously avoid the alternative—the sacrifice is too great. B. is engaged on Saturday (8).

div.head: 1204.—Saturday, September 28, 1861.
div.p: TOM MOORE.—This day’s post gives great hopes, is quite encouraging. You arrange in every way as you deem most prudent. We begin to anticipate the results of your almost certain success (9).

div.head: 1205.—Wednesday, October 2, 1861.
div.p: SERPENT—Dove.—Bedford.—Geranium.—Just RECEIVED, FIRST SIGNAL, unknown to the rest. Write it me, and let me answer you. Quite right so far. Annie, dear, good-night.—M. T. South Norwood—Glove—size.

div.head: 1206.—Tuesday, October 8, 1861.
div.p: G.P. L.—Virtue, honour, perseverance, will bring elevation and deserts, and, it is hoped, forgiveness.—GRIEF.

div.head: 1207.—Tuesday, October 8, 1861.
div.p: UNCLE TOM.—If you have not already written, pray WRITE, as there is very much anxiety. You may see B. any day, from 2 till 4, and later if requisite (1).

div.head: 1208.—Thursday, October 10, 1861.
div.p: BELLA, St. Mary’s, must see G. H., or hear from them immediately. Something must be settled before the winter. Bad season. Ill health. What was suggested will be the best plan to adopt. Make an advance, it is an effort, but will eventually prove the best for all. Parties surrounded by enemies. Don’t hesitate. Inevitable ruin is the result.

div.head: 1209.—Friday, October 11, 1861.
div.p: INFELIX.—Notice of your return vainly expected. Ire. to H. V. 11th, Spring 15th and Home 18th, unless——. Send your plans directly chez moi. O. will forward them. Birdie much wanted. Work nearly done. Esperanza. Addio. Yours, T.

div.head: 1210.—Thursday, October 17, 1861.
div.p: UNCLE TOM.—Yes, received. We are well. For you we are painfully anxious. Your happiness is inseparable from our own. Spare nothing to obtain the one result so important to your future. B. will let you have anything you require to ensure that. He longs to see you here or there. Is anything settled in regard to the holydays? Think of the commencement of this month (2).

div.head: 1211.—Monday, November 11, 1861.
div.p: PERCY.—Was it not abominable of you? Poor M. was greatly disappointed. Pity her a little.

div.head: 1212.—Wednesday, November 13, 1861.
div.p: MAIBLUMCHEN, schriebe du sogleich das du dies gesehen habest, will ich wie gewohnlich einen Brief schreiben.

div.head: 1213.—Wednesday, November 20, 1861.
div.p: XMAS.—Happy birthday.

div.head: 1214.—Wednesday, November 20, 1861.
div.p: EVANGELIST.—Rightly done.—M. O. M.

div.head: 1215.—Thursday, November 21, 1861.
div.p: WITH remorse and misery beyond telling, I find myself alone. Be merciful! Pray let me send what money you want, it would be the greatest consolation. God bless!—C. . .

div.head: 1216.—Friday, November 22, 23, 1861.
div.p: LITTLE SILLY.—Under cover to my Agent.

div.head: 1217.—Monday, November 25, 1861.
div.p: KLEPTOMANIA’S silly COMMUNICATION RECEIVED.

div.head: 1218.—Monday, November 25, 1861.
div.p: GIOIA MIA.—Do not prejudge me. Wait for my letter. I was mad, ma fidèle. A thousand thanks for all. Je suis bien triste.

div.head: 1219.—Tuesday, December 3, 5, 7, 1861.
div.p: DEAR OLD MONSTER.—Little Ling is very unhappy. Horse is well.

div.head: 1220.—Thursday, December 5, 1861.
div.p: 05100.—Moribond.—3rd Dec. 1861. Abruzzi, 13.—Hotel des Ambassadeurs.—Ig. Pollaky.

div.head: 1221.—Saturday, December 7, 1861.
div.p: Y.Z.—To-day there has been “sunshine through the clouds.” I shall call, as before, in case. ARGUS. December 6.

div.head: 1222.—Saturday, December 7, 1861.
div.p: MY dear HARRY.—Look at our old friend Jupiter, and have faith in your kind old sister, LIZZY.

div.head: 1223.—Tuesday, December 10, 1861.
div.p: C.A. G.—Do not send any more till I see you. Fresher than ever. Quite well. N. S.

div.head: 1224.—Tuesday, December 10, 1861.
div.p: 05100.—Moribond.—Abruzzi, 9th December, 1861. Tempora mutantur, et nos mutamur in illis. Ab uno disce omnes.—IGNATIUS POLLAKY.

div.head: 1225.—Thursday, December 12, 1861.
div.p: 05100.—Moribond—Abruzzi.—11th December, 61.—Your COMMUNICATION RECEIVED. The arguments entirely irrelevant to the point in question.—IGNATIUS POLLAKY.

div.head: 1226.—Friday, December 13, 1861.
div.p: UNCLE TOM.—Pray WRITE. Is it impossible to get to B. this week? These disappointments are very sad (3).

div.head: 1227.—Thursday, December 19, 1861.
div.p: INSOMUCH as ye have done it unto one of the least of these, my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Thanks—thanks.

div.head: 1228.—Friday, January 3, 1862.
div.p: FAITH CROWNS ALL; seal Dec. 31, communication received from an “Old Friend.” An interview or card of address requested. Address as the last.—J. D.

div.head: 1229.—Wednesday, January 8, 1862.
div.p: CÆSAR J.—He is very unhappy at having pained others, and, in spite of all appearances, is loyal and true. The pilgrim is sad and desolate, but hopes not to be forgotten. Bless her and both children. Revda rof tuo Kool.

div.head: 1230.—Wednesday, January 15, 1862.
div.p: 0’503,Ad captandum vulgus.—She has arrived, but dangerously ill. Forgive. You can have the necessary guarantees on applying to Mr. Pollaky, Private Continental Inquiry-office, 14, George-street, Mansion House.

div.head: 1231.—Tuesday, January 28, 1862.
div.p: CÆSAR J.—The absence and silence of his children cause much sorrow to the pilgrim. He hopes to hear soon. The usual address. Bless them both. He cannot change.

div.head: 1232.—Tuesday, January 28, 1862.
div.p: WATCHER.—Dismiss all doubts. No one can supply your place. Absence strengthens the tie. I look so steadfastly to the future, and approve all your plans.

div.head: 1233.—Wednesday, February 5, 1862.
div.p: S——L H——L.—I promise. The 3rd or 10th of March. One there now.—C., Feb. 3, 1862.

div.head: 1234.—Thursday, February 13, 1862.
div.p: OUR TERRACE.—My Beloved, I live only in the assurance of your truth and love. Pray WRITE.

div.head: 1235.—Friday, February 14, 1862.
div.p: G.O. in D.—Very good for false premises. Try again, but let truth be your guide. Dublin.

div.head: 1236.—Friday, February 14, 1862.
div.p: WATCHER.—All safe. WRITE, and send the letter. Do not be alarmed, as the object of the writers must be to annoy or intimidate you for some purpose of their own. Their malice here is quite harmless. Above all, make no confidant, nor ask any advice. Be patient, and rely upon me. An unexpected absence has caused this delay. For ever ——.

div.head: 1237.—Wednesday, February 26, 1862.
div.p: FRED.—All right. I sympathize with your pain, but why seek consolation where you cannot find it, and in a way that pains me? WRITE as usual. Trust ever.

div.head: 1238.—Saturday, March 8, 1862.
div.p: H.S. S.—RECEIVED your LETTER. Have twice advertised. Utterly useless to accept an engagement. Not much success. Nearly four months. No tidings from my friend. This is the worst trouble. Expenses very heavy. Write soon.

div.head: 1239.—Thursday, March 13, 1862.
div.p: IT was once bare! Should he have taken it? Is the chance gone?—from WATCHER.

div.head: 1240.—Friday, March 14, 1862.
div.p: WATCHER.—Your long silence has caused me much suffering. Are you ill? I can hardly think so, as you promised to send for me. I anxiously await some reply.

div.head: 1241.—Tuesday, March 25, 1862.
div.p: CÆSAR J.—The Pilgrim is much distressed at the long silence of his children. Can they not let him hear through his family. When do they return? He is unchanging. Is he forgotten?

div.head: 1242.—Wednesday, March 26, 1862.
div.p: FRED.—The dog has always been with me and is still. Save anxiety for your health. I am very happy. Your hopes are mine, and I fervently say amen to them. You are dearer than ever so close.

div.head: 1243.—Tuesday, April 1, 1862.
div.p: REVELATIONS.—19th chapter, 4th verse. England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland into 24 provinces—Genesis, 1st chapter, 27th verse—to each province of districts, 0 to 9, and guilds 0 to 9, the companies 00 to 09, and 10 to 99, common to both.

div.head: 1244.—Tuesday, April 29, 1862.
div.p: TO R. N.—Wedding Cake. Spanish Knife. Awoke picking up tips of fingers. Is it a sign of my fall from the height which I fain would climb?—H. C.

div.head: 1245.—Wednesday, May 7, 1862.
div.p: LIKE a SHIP WITHOUT a RUDDER, in apparent calm, she will SINK without aid. Give some sign.

div.head: 1246.—Wednesday, May 7, 1862.
div.p: A.E. S.—I have not heard from you for a week, and have no idea where you are. N’import—“Where ignorance is bliss,” etc., and Patti is really charming. London, Tuesday.

div.head: 1247.—Friday, May 9, 1862.
div.p: W.W. S.—Zy epfdlj I dpye wpeepc ez mjcyp qzc jzf—xlj I daplv qfwwj zy lww xleepcd le esp tyepcgtph? te xlj oz Rzzo ecfde ez xj wzgp—I lx xtdpclmwp—hspy xlj I rz ez nlyepcmfcj tq zywj ez wzzv le jzf.—May 8.

div.head: 1248.—Monday, May 12, 1862.
div.p: W.W. S.—Sxhrdktg hdbtiwxjv “Imwxqxixde axyt” udg—. Pcdewtg psktgexhtbtci.—Q N G C T.

div.head: 1249.—Tuesday, May 13, 1862.
div.p: TY D E L D.—zq zzlyz ez nlyepcmfcj, I estyv jzf sld xfns mpiipc delj le syxp lyd xtyd jzfc mfdtypdd.—W W S., May 10.

div.head: 1250.—Tuesday, May 13, 1862.
div.p: W.W. S.—Fyetw jzfc qlespc lydpcd I hzye ldv jzf ez aczgp jzf wzgp xpepfdlj ytrse le yyp znwznv slgp l dectyr qczx esp htyozh qzc wpeeped Iq jzf lcp yze lmwp le zyp I htww hlte. Rzo nzxqzce jzf xj olcwtyr htqp.

div.head: 1251.—Wednesday, May 14, 1862.
div.p: POUSSE.—RETURN at once. I have squared everything. The maternal has not yet heard. The monoptic will kill the fatted calf. Another day the news will have reached home. Come to dinner at 7 to-night.

div.head: 1252.—Friday, May 16, 1862.
div.p: THE NONCE’S DREAM.—RETURN, or you will kill your mother. No one yet knows your absence, and I have squared everything. Write for any money you want.—The Monoptic L, and the Artist.

div.head: 1253.—Monday, June 2, 1862.
div.p: FOUR.—Inadmissible, but all well in every way. Will meditate and think. It can probably be done.—C. F.

div.head: 1254.—Thursday, June 12, 13, 14, 1862.
div.p: CHAFFINCH.—January Wife.—Must die unless you go at once home to Garden of the Soul. No one will know. Besides M. can assure C. all can be made right and forgiven.

div.head: 1255.—Thursday, July 3, 1862.
div.p: THREE. Your conduct is admirable. Wait. Events unfold themselves best.

div.head: 1256.—Wednesday, July 9, 1862.
div.p: IT is easy to find a brother, not so a kind friend.

div.head: 1257.—Monday, July 21, 1862.
div.p: Z.B.—Finis coronat opus. 15th July, 1862. Pollaky.

div.head: 1258.—Tuesday, July 22, 1862.
div.p: M.to G.—He has sneezed.—St. J.’s. July 20.

div.head: 1259.—Thursday, July 31, 1862.
div.p: PENCIL.—Should I take old R——g? Answer J. P. A. T. 7.7.7.7.

div.head: 1260.—Thursday, July 31, 1862.
div.p: INFELIX.—T. wants to communicate with Bird. Arrange with Ce and let me know, through Springwell or direct, before the 7th, when T. leaves town for Springs. N. & Co. go to B. S. shortly, I hear.

div.head: 1261.—Wednesday, August 13, 1862.
div.p: LONDON, Aug. 11, 1862. E.C. No. 226.

div.head: 1262.—Wednesday, August 20, 1862.
div.p: PRUSSIA, August 19.—All safe.—Robert Henry.

div.head: 1263.—Thursday, August 28, 1862.
div.p: BRUGES to Turk.—Who’s a hound? Write to town. T. G.

div.head: 1264.—Friday, August 29, 1862.
div.p: IDA.—Do not act as you propose. It would be madness, and could only end in misery, worse than any you dream of. Be brave; our fate is much of our own making. We send you our blessing.—The Pope.

div.head: 1265.—Friday, September 19, 1862.
div.p: C.S.—N——y—. Again, or good-bye, &c. E——r E., S.M.C.

div.head: 1266.—Saturday, September 20, 1862.
div.p: A.Z.—“La nuée a crevé sur nous.” J’erre tout seul dans le bois, mais je te trouverai à la fin. Je sais à qui je me fie mille fois mieux que ceux qui ont fait de si vains efforts pour ébranler la confiance que j’ai en toi. Nous ne deviendrons que plus proche de Dieu et plus chers l’un à l’autre par suite de toute cette douleur, et je te prie de n’abandonner jamais ta FAITH.

div.head: 1267.—Thursday, September 25, 1862.
div.p: MINERVA.—What a pretty little seal!

div.head: 1268.—Thursday, September 25, 1862.
div.p: AZIM.—Remember your child’s first and last words. Are they not true? MARIE.

div.head: 1269.—Thursday, September 25, 1862.
div.p: JE N’OUBLIERAI JAMAIS ta MÈRE.—Les liens invisibles sont les plus sacrés. Soyez heureuse. Sept. 29, 1862. Ap. 28. N. 6, 13. Je n’écriverai plus.

div.head: 1270.—Thursday, October 2, 1862.
div.p: A.Z.—Est-ce-que je te deplais en me rendant à ——? Je tâcherai à m’absenter si tu le désires véritablement, mais il faut que tu m’en avertise. Je ne crois pas à la rumeur; elle a dit de toi ce qui ne peut pas être vrai. Quant à moi, crois seulement que j’ai toujours en toi une confiance inébranlable, et que je garde religieusement ma parole. Donne-moi tes prières, j’en ai besoin. Tu as toujours les miennes. Voir The Times de samedi, le 20 septembre.—FAITH.

div.head: 1271.—Monday, October 6, 1862.
div.p: AMAZON.—P.O., Oxford.

div.head: 1272.—Tuesday, October 7, 1862.
div.p: A.Z.—Ma Faith ne peut me déplaire; elle est bien bonne de ne pas faire attention à ces histoires; elle sait qu’on ne connait que trop bien l’espérance de ma vie, et veut se venger en la détruisant; mais j’aime ma Faith, et vienne que vienne je l’aimerai pour toujours. Allons donc, pas plus de doutes, le bon Dieu bénira nos volontés, et tout ira bien à la fin.

div.head: 1273.—Thursday, October 9, 1862.
div.p: SEMPER IDEM.—WRITE or COME, nothing doubting. June 1855. 1 Thess. chap. 11, verse 19.—FAITH.

div.head: 1274.—Friday, October 10, 1862.
div.p: GEORGE.—A fair start after a long walk. DO COME or WRITE, to relieve this anxiety.

div.head: 1275.—Saturday, October 11, 1862.
div.p: JE n’oublierai jamais ta Mère.—Ap. 26, 27, 30, 1850. M. 4, 11. Les liens invisible sont les plus sacrés—N. 6. 13. Les enfants me laissent peu de loisir, jamais ne peut-on conter sur un jour de fête, toujours il arrive quelque contretemps; mais, je ne suis pas malade, et, si Dieu permet, j’espère me rendre à W. N. 2nd, passer le dimanche près de mon vieux toit paternal. Je suis fâché qu’une lettre écrite (il y a quelques semaines) dans une langue étrangère vous n’a pas trouvée, car je n’aime pas ce mode d’entretien. Mon amitié ne changera jamais, mais je n’écriverai plus de ce façon.—Ap. 28, N. 6, 13.

div.head: 1276.—Thursday, October 23, 1862.
div.p: HOPE.—The MISSING ONE is RECEIVED. Your two last darlings have done me good, and I cannot but trust you. My feelings are more intense than ever. Cast away those presentiments of evil that you tell me about, and believe me unchanged. Write as often as you can. My wishes fly to unite with yours.

div.head: 1277.—Monday, October 27, 1862.
div.p: OFT expectation fails, and most oft there Where most it promises; and oft it hits, When hope is coldest, and despair most sits.

div.head: 1278.—Tuesday, October 28, 29, 30, 31, November 1, 6, 7, 1862.
div.p: SOMEBODY’S LUGGAGE.

div.head: 1279.—Wednesday, October 29, 1862.
div.p: X.EGGS. X.

div.head: 1280.—Wednesday, October 29, 1862.
div.p: AMAZON RECEIVED.

div.head: 1281.—Wednesday, October 27, 1862.
div.p: HOPE. I like your last very much. How can you doubt me ? I had written to you, but the party you mention thought better of it, and declined to forward it. I am dying to see you, that we may settle matters. I am better than I was, and look forward to happier days.

div.head: 1282.—Thursday, October 30, 1862.
div.p: X.SILK X.

div.head: 1283.—Friday, October 31, 1862.
div.p: FIDES (Thought).—No myth, but a neighbouring town, where I shall be detained a little time. I shall be in for a few hours on Monday, and must take my chance of meeting you between 2 and 3 o’clock. Perhaps I may hear from you meantime. Direct to P.O.

div.head: 1284.—Saturday, November 1, 1862.
div.p: M.A. Y.

div.head: 1285.—Saturday, November 1, 1862.
div.p: X.CAEN X.

div.head: 1286.—Tuesday, November 4, 1862.
div.p: XWIRTHSHAUS X—Key—X Eggs X—X Silk X—X Caen X (×. plus) X Wirthshaus X = X Tour X.

div.head: 1287.—Tuesday, November 4, 1862.
div.p: A.Z.—Je me suis tenu éloigné de——à cause de toi. Ne juge pas mal de mon absence. Les choses que l’on t’a ôté, je les garderai précieusement jusqu’à ce que tu pourras les réclamer. Fais-moi savoir si cette voie-ci de communication me reste toujours ouverte. Ruth, ch. i. vs. 16, 17.—FAITH.

div.head: 1288.—Wednesday, November 5, 1862.
div.p: BAMBOROUGH—QUITE RIGHT.

div.head: 1289.—Wednesday, November 5, 1862.
div.p: HOPE.—If you can forgive me for my unkindness, let me know when I can write to you, and communicate my plans.

div.head: 1290.—Friday, November 7, 8, 1862.
div.p: CANTERBURY.—We are waiting. Come. No questions will be asked. Lots of fun, Nov. 5. Hockham.

div.head: 1291.—Tuesday, November 11, 1862.
div.p: A.Z.—Je t’aime trop à te juger. Fais comme tu es convenable. Il suffit de me rendre heureux à voir ou même à penser à ma belle, bonne, heureuse. FAITH.

div.head: 1292.—Wednesday, November 12, 1862.
div.p: AQUIET EVENING and a LITTLE Music.

div.head: 1293.—Friday, November 14, 1862.
div.p: FIDES (invisible).—All to hand I suppose, indicating initial missing. Thanks. The sleeping partnership affair was known to me some time ago, and I hinted it to your senior, though I could not speak of it. I am glad, though surprised, that you accept it with equanimity. Your liability being limited, however, I hope you will not suffer much, and it cannot be undone now. If you send on Saturday, let it be to same address, I shall be at No. 3 on Monday. Carl has been confined again, but is better: he has received urgent calls from abroad, but he seems as stupidly obstinate as ever he was in his life, and I have little hope of improvement in him. Southampton matters look lively.

div.head: 1294.—Saturday, November 15, 1862.
div.p: BAMBOROUGH—RECEIVED.

div.head: 1295.—Saturday, November 22, 1862.
div.p: F.a F.—Off to-day, 17th. Do not U. S. but R.P.R. Return uncertain. S. would do.

div.head: 1296.—Monday, November 24, 1862.
div.p: BAMBOROUGH—RECEIVED—Grateful thanks.

div.head: 1297.—Tuesday, November 25, 27, 28, 1862.
div.p: CHROMO—FULGENT!

div.head: 1298.—Thursday, November 27, 1862.
div.p: HYDRA—Guards—Gorilla—Hand.—What has become of this? Though apparently forsaken early, the interest I felt in it remains undiminished. Still M. T. P.O., Nina, South Norwood.

div.head: 1299.—Monday, December 1, 1862.
div.p: NEVER SAY DIE.—All alone in my glory. Try again. Give me the dates of your two last. Change the place.

div.head: 1300.—Friday, December 5, 1862.
div.p: FELIX.—Limpet must stick fast till 12th January. Springwell continues. I. was right, and Jup’s grumble nonsense. Agreed, “more pain than pleasure” at the gathering. I pray you write T. by 16th. Taking steps. Be firm, true, and God bless you.

div.head: 1301.—Friday, December 5, 1862.
div.p: A.Z.—Je suis aise de savoir que tu te portes bien. Tout ce qu’on a dit et fait n’a pas ébranlé ma confiance en toi. Les dernières paroles ont pour moi plus de poids que tout ce que personne peut dire on faire. Mon destin est entre tes mains. Je ne manquerai pas à mon vœu.—FAITH.

div.head: 1302.—Thursday, December 18, 1862.
div.p: SPURS and SKIRTS.—Page 296, lines 10, 11, 12. Garibaldi. Pio Nono.

div.head: 1303.—Friday, December 19, 1862.
div.p: SPURS and SKIRTS.—Page 154, lines 14, 15. Anita Pope Joan.

div.head: 1304.—Saturday, December 20, 1862.
div.p: SPURS and SKIRTS.—The father of E— W— informs Garibaldi Pio Nono that all is discovered and any attempts to renew the correspondence futile, Spurs and Skirts and the Times being forbidden at S— Lodge.

div.head: 1305.—Thursday, January 1, 1863.
div.p: A.Z.—Je te souhais “bien des retours heureux de ce jour” (tu sais que je le manquerais plus dignement s’il était possible) et “que le nouvel an te soit heureux.” Le vieux a assez de tristes souvenirs pour nous. J’étais à —— Noël: quel contraste avec celui de l’an 1861! Dieu veuille que l’année qui vient de commencer nous rende tous deux à l’ancien bonheur; je ne doute pas qu’il ne revienne un jour si nous continuons à mettre notre confiance en Dieu, et à avoir foi l’un à l’autre.—2 Cor. vii., 16. FAITH.

div.head: 1306.—Monday, January 5, 1863.
div.p: NIL DESPERANDUM.—Pray WRITE immediately, and tell me what H—r said, and what you answered or promised. You tell me nothing. What you ask is impossible. I told you I could not come again in the way you propose. If you wish it as much as I do, it must be the old plan. Write. I am worse than you are. Settle something. What a bore hats are.

div.head: 1307.—Thursday, January 8, 1863.
div.p: SMALL HOUSE—Danger. Cross the sea.

div.head: 1308.—Friday, January 9, 1863.
div.p: NIL DESPERANDUM.—If your feelings are what you describe, why do you not WRITE oftener or arrange something? What must mine be? Do next Monday what you did last Monday. A happy new year to you! It rests with yourself.

div.head: 1309.—Friday, January 16, 1863.
div.p: NIL DESPERANDUM.—Thank you. How can you think they bore me? I will be there according to your appointment, but hope to see you before if possible.

div.head: 1310.—Wednesday, January 21, 1863.
div.p: SQUIRE TREVLYN’S Heir.

div.head: 1311.—Wednesday, January 21, 1863.
div.p: EDWARD STREET—NELSON.

div.head: 1312.—Thursday, January 22, 1863.
div.p: NIL DESPERANDUM.—RECEIVED the DOCUMENTS so effaced as to be almost unintelligible. Floss wishes you to WRITE here unreservedly; there is no risk; she will take care the letter only falls into Tiney’s hands. Never doubted you.

div.head: 1313.—Friday, January 30, 31, 1863.
div.p: X.X. X.

div.head: 1314.—Wednesday, February 4, 1863.
div.p: DAVIS.—Correspondence must cease. The alliance is wrong. Active measures, more explicit if needed—when directing friends. Will deliver you from Bartholomew—J.D. K.V.

div.head: 1315.—Thursday, February 5, 1863.
div.p: A.Z.—J’aime à croire que nous avons tous deux les mêmes “Stunden der Andacht” (dans plus d’un sens). Sans des anticipations de jours plus heureux à l’avenir, ma vie, maintenant solitaire et ennuyante, serait tout-à-fait misérable. Je puis attendre sans promesse, mais non pas sans espoir; je puis rester sans assurance, mais point sans—FAITH.

div.head: 1316.—Tuesday, February 10, 14, 16, 17, 1863.
div.p: X.X. X.—Wednesday.

div.head: 1317.—Monday, March 2, 1863.
div.p: YOUR ROOM.—It is as I told you, it would be the night I last saw you. Too sad; too unhappy; too wretched. Each day, if possible, worse than the last. If I dared I wish all were over. I would give up all and everything for eau de Cologne once more. February 9th. Look again May 1st. Take care of yourself dear A.

div.head: 1318.—Thursday, March 5, 1863.
div.p: A.Z.—J’ai reçu les trois PORTRAITS, C. d. V. Tu t’amuseras un jour, au récit des détails. (Que c’est bon de la part des enfants!) Le tien m’a mis en état de finir un portrait à trois-quarts de la grandeur naturelle qui a été quelques mois en état de progrès. Tu sais à cause de qui je me rende si rarement à ——. Je me trouve forcé de m’y rendre quelquefois. Je souhais que cette année triste et ennuyeuse se passe. Les souvenirs du passé me défendent d’être autre que plein d’espérance joyeuse pour l’avenir. A parler humainement, notre destin est sous ta garde; et je suis content, en confiance affectionnée, de la laisser là. Que Dieu te bénisse!—FAITH.

div.head: 1319.—Tuesday, March 10, 1863.
div.p: INFELIX.—With mingled fear and hope. T. beseeches Bird to remember promises for future conduct, so lately made. WRITE how Limpet’s health is. Springwell forwards. List 3 is done. Take care! Be true and steadfast, and may God bless you!—T.

div.head: 1320.—Thursday, March 19, 1863.
div.p: INFELIX.—Why is Inf. of 10th neglected? Yesterday was remembered. Account of Limpet’s state and doings earnestly desired. Springwell continues. T. not quite well. Tell Bird to go to H. V. when asked. Remember 21st, and please attend to this.

div.head: 1321.—Monday, March 30, 1863.
div.p: SALVEO PEDES.

div.head: 1322.—Wednesday, April 1, 7, 1863.
div.p: SALVEO PEDES.

div.head: 1323.—Saturday, April 4, 1863.
div.p: A.Z.—J’ai une belle nouvelle pour toi. Un second paquet est arrivé; on a tâché de faire croire que tu l’avais envoyé, mais on ne nous a pas trompé comme ça. Il les embarrasse sans cesse, que de garder ton secret comme tu le fais. Cela ne réussirait fas s’ils te comprenaient aussi bien que moi. J’essayerai de te voir bientôt, car je veux te consulter sur le projet d’aller à——l’été prochain, et sur d’autres affaires plus importantes. Quelques efforts qu’ils fassent, ils n’ébranleront point la foi que je mets en toi. Fais que je sache quand tu vas aller au bord de la mer. Que Dieu te bénisse.—FAITH.

div.head: 1324.—Tuesday, April 14, 1863.
div.p: TURF.—If you respect my opinion keep away from him. In London I hear no good. Delicacy must not prevent you communicating exact details. I will not reproach, but assist you. Your misery is mine. Did you get books? He must be there if I am. Select.

div.head: 1325.—Thursday, April 16, 1863.
div.p: CAN I dare to write again until I am certain of . . . . and where? . . . Can I forget the sad request of your last!

div.head: 1326.—Friday, April 24, 1863.
div.p: TURF.—I am anxious to hear you have seen the Times of April 14th. Do you wish me to go there next month? Will the objectionable person be there? Confide in me.

div.head: 1327.—Friday, May 1, 1863.
div.p: F.F.—Naples, Paris, or elsewhere. G. Smith’s on 15th. Not twins this time.

div.head: 1328.—Wednesday, May 6, 1863.
div.p: A——.—Lat. 41 degrees N., long. 10 degrees W.—Pollaky, 4th May, 1863.

div.head: 1329.—Wednesday, May 20, 1863.
div.p: THE DERBY TURNPIKE TICKET.

div.head: 1330.—Friday, May 22, 1863.
div.p: ZERO.—Epsom—to the north 4 to 5. “Nous verrons.”—POLLAKY.

div.head: 1331.—Saturday, June 6, 1863.
div.p: A.Z.—Je vais expliquer l’omission du mois passé quand l’occasion s’offria. J’ai été encore une fois à P——h! Le serment de ce jour là reste, et restera à jamais inviolable. J’entends d’étranges rumeurs, mais je sais qu’elles ne peuvent pas être vraies. Je rejette tout ce qui ne s’accorde pas avec tes derniers mots. Je viens de constater une circonstance toute particulière, qui fait abondamment voir ton désaveu de certains procedés recent; si même j’en avais jamais douté. Quelles que soient les rumeurs qui te viennent, crois seulement à ma confiance et ma fidélité inébranlables.—FAITH.

div.head: 1332.—Friday, June 12, 1863.
div.p: Z.—The old doctrine of “being within the four seas” would not affect the final issue of the case.—POLLAKY.

div.head: 1333.—Friday, June 12, 1863.
div.p: TURF.—A month has passed since we met. The photograph not sent, or letter received. To neglect a sincere friend is foolish and unkind. Write explicitly. I hate uncertainty. Are we to meet again?

div.head: 1334.—Thursday, June 18, 1863.
div.p: Z.—Just soon enough to be too late; with a secret which is no secret after all.—POLLAKY.

div.head: 1337.—Wednesday, July 1, 1863.
div.p: TURF.—The information did not reach me in time for the request to be complied with. COMMUNICATE again.

div.head: 1338.—Thursday, July 9, 1863.
div.p: A.Z.—“Thy will be done.”—FAITH.

div.head: 1339.—Monday, July 13, 14, 1863.
div.p: THERE is happiness in calm resignation.—Lam. iii. 3-7. No. 13. “Thy will be done.”

div.head: 1340.—Thursday, August 6, 1863.
div.p: ALFRED.—COME, oh, come. I beseech a last interview. Remember the 25th. Although I am bound in honour and in justice to myself to give all up then, yet I am willing to make the sacrifice, and will hand you the greatest number. I desire to spare, if not your feelings, at least those of some one else.

div.head: 1341.—Thursday, August 13, 1863.
div.p: VIOLET TOKEN!—Your conduct was most unaccountable, and towards “——” most unjust. Your letters await only your honourable explanation being given to him. He’s waited long, patiently, and at great loss. WRITE to him immediately, with confidential explanations, by post—fear not. Or write, as formerly, through those who passed your many previous letters. Act on this advice honourably, and without delay. All shall end as you wish. Pocket-book, with portraits.

div.head: 1342.—Friday, August 14, 1863.
div.p: TURF.—WRITE. It is long since I heard from you. Since we met last I have had much trouble. When can we meet again? Brighton this autumn?

div.head: 1343.—Tuesday, August 25, 1863.
div.p: SAINT SWITHIN is so very sorry! Was the paragraph intended for him?

div.head: 1344.—Friday, August 28, 1863.
div.p: THY WILL BE DONE—the language of heaven echoed on earth.—August 27. “We praise thee, O Lord.”

div.head: 1345.—Monday, September 14, 1863.
div.p: MIGHT, Could, Would, and Should—“The many only formed one ——”! Is W. Hand’s address known?

div.head: 1346.—Saturday, September 19, 1863.
div.p: MR. A. G.—“Oui.” Bien fermé. V. dévoué A. F.

div.head: 1347.—Wednesday, September 23, 1863.
div.p: ONUTA.—Might, Could ——? “The many only formed one.” Send the right address to W. Hand.

div.head: 1348.—Tuesday, September 29, 1863.
div.p: FRANKFORT MINE. One blank. One prize. One month, Treasure. Been to sea.

div.head: 1349.—Thursday, October 1, 1863.
div.p: TURF.—Why so long silent? No reply to last advertisement. Where can we meet? My time is not at my own disposal, or I would long ago have seen you.

div.head: 1350.—Wednesday, October 7, 1863.
div.p: PHILIP. i. 3. June 13th, 1863—“Aimée pour soi-même, aimée malgré soi-même.” V. H. LM II. 68. Voilà une conviction qui s’établit difficilement dans le cœur, ou que l’ennemi du genre humain s’occupe sournoisement à dénouer les cordes qui nous enchainent l’un à l’autre, à nous soustraire à ces communions légitimes et benies, avant-couriers d’une heureuse éternité. Complice dans le passé de ce pouvoir ténébreux, tremblante à ce moment-ci, fidèle maintenant et à jamais, détourne de moi les maux que j’ai mérités très justement, car mon âme est à genoux.—SUPPLICATION.

div.head: 1351.—Thursday, October 15, 16, 1863.
div.p: WHERE are TRUTH and HONOUR?

div.head: 1352.—Tuesday, October 20, 1863.
div.p: TRUTH and HONOUR UNIMPAIRED. Inquire at Clifton Post-office.

div.head: 1353.—Wednesday, October 21, 1863.
div.p: SIC VOLO, SIC JUBEO, &c. Di. Di. Unterzeichne die Quittung, sonst die Qual der Armuth sollst du erleiden, “Gott sey deiner Seele-gnädigehrloser Mann.”—Breslau.

div.head: 1354.—Tuesday, October 27, 1863.
div.p: WARMINSTER.—Wake up Kirby! Write to your afflicted Jim!

div.head: 1355.—Saturday, November 21, 1863.
div.p: TURF.—Your long silence is cruel. Why has not photo been sent, and no notice been taken of last two advertisements? Where do you spend Christmas? When can we meet?

div.head: 1356.—Friday, November 27, 28, 1863.
div.p: THE name explains the lost meaning—Answer. Yeovil. E.

div.head: 1357.—Friday, December 18, 1863.
div.p: FELIX.—Take the end opposite and furthest from that at which you enter. Does Ce. keep documents again? I will observe Bird’s directions, and be generally prudent. Limpet need not fear. Merry Christmas and Happy New Year to you.

div.head: 1358.—Friday, December 25, 1863.
div.p: FELIX.—192 is safe. Inform T. of change of day, or plan, not later than by post from you of Saturday. Address at Orph’s direct. The recent notice related to Bird’s projected flight, and not to Terpsichore.

div.head: 1359.—Tuesday, December 29, 1863.
div.p: MONKEY.—Six, thirty.

div.head: 1360.—Friday, January 1, 1864.
div.p: SIESTA.—A. or P. in W. or W. Yes, always. F. & D. M. O. D. Sure. A happy new year.

div.head: 1361.—Monday, February 1, 1864.
div.p: FRANK.—A, Yes. B, No. C, Believe no. D, Will try. F, Doubtful; payments disputed. G, Much distressed, considers, wants further news. J. K. H., well. L, vexed; also disputed.

div.head: 1362.—Saturday, February 6, 1864.
div.p: TURF.—Many thanks. Why so long silent? Have been dangerously ill—still unwell; therefore could not come or communicate. Hope to meet soon. WRITE. Photo never sent.

div.head: 1363.—Friday, February 12, 1864.
div.p: KISMET.—Incognita, trésor de mon âme, comblée de malheur, mais à vous toujours.—A. G.

div.head: 1364.—Monday, February 15, 1864.
div.p: INCOGNITA.—Carissima! si c’est bien vous, écrivez (comme auparavant), je vous en supplie. Ina costante.—KISMET.

div.head: 1365.—Saturday, February 27, 1864.
div.p: WAS it really your own wish—your own plan? . . . . . I did not deserve it! . . . I cannot so soon forget, but I have forgiven! Unless you mention something known to us only, I shall never consider it yours.—LOST L——.

div.head: 1366.—Tuesday, March 1, 1864.
div.p: M.N.—You are dearly loved, and always will be. All are kind. We are well.—Q. by A.

div.head: 1367.—Thursday, March 3, 1864.
div.p: JleM.—Forgiven, never forgotten. Your heart and thoughts belong to another. Your future: a happy one. . . . Mine? . . .

div.head: 1368.—Monday, March 7, 1864.
div.p: CITE.—Oh! that impression of yours is most wrong! Another? . . . . There is no proof that I would refuse you, were you only to ask—you know my address—why will you not? Do, and then judge me!—D. C. (pencil).

div.head: 1369.—Friday, March 11, 1864.
div.p: SHOOT RIGHT AT HIM.—The game is yours alone—at present he is powerless—Je vous aime.

div.head: 1370.—Tuesday, March 22, 26, 1864.
div.p: S.L. R.—The event you expect may be long delayed. It is quite vain to wait. If you arrange now, you can save yourself and help me. Neglect this, and I shall go into seclusion immediately. All will then be over. Communicate as before, or through the Times, to E. C.

div.head: 1371.—Friday, April 1, 1864.
div.p: M.N.—Truly sincerely loved. Affliction brings love in its truest form. Hope reigns strong.—Q. by A.

div.head: 1372.—Tuesday, April 12, 1864.
div.p: INFELIX FELIX.—The EASTER OFFERING was RECEIVED, and greatly valued. Although most unfounded and unkind, J’s mammonish opinion of T. matters not, save for its effect on you. Business progresses fairly. Be trustful, and doubt not that matters will surely come right. Arrange with Ce. in three or four weeks if possible. Ch. has parcel for Bird.

div.head: 1373.—Thursday, April 14, 1864.
div.p: NINNI. Gedenkest du der Rosenkrone? HUGO.

div.head: 1375.—Friday, April 29, 1864.
div.p: TURF.—At great inconvenience I visited P— on Tuesday morning and afternoon, also Wednesday afternoon. A long interview is much desired. WRITE soon. Disappointment great.

div.head: 1376.—Saturday, April 30, 1864.
div.p: TO J. S.—I did not take advice until after you sent me word you had gone. I have only informed our medical friend here. I have taken charge of part of your lambs, the rest stray till Monday. I will try to keep your absence secret till then. What must I do?—E. S., N. Wales.

div.head: 1377.—Monday, May 23, 1864.
div.p: QUIEN SABE?—Pictures,—Kind NOTE of 10th only just FOUND. Out of town. Much regret. Please write again. Put some address.—H.

div.head: 1378.—Friday, May 27, 1864.
div.p: NOBODY.—Cigar Case Daily.—Do WRITE.

div.head: 1379.—Wednesday, June 1, 1864.
div.p: M.N.—Anxiety is most painful; is there nothing to alleviate it? Just the same. The old, old story.—Q. by A.

div.head: 1380.—Thursday, June 9, 1864.
div.p: QUIEN SABE? 1. Pictures. “Look at the Cat”—the Serpent and the Stork. “Civet.” Moses Scourged. “The Binding of the Dragon. A Shark’s Mouth.” “The Dog Barks.” “The Wolf and the Lamb.” “I introduce an old Acquaintance.” Major Ker—Callander.

div.head: 1381.—Friday, June 10, 1864.
div.p: MARIE.

div.head: 1382.—Friday, June 10, 1864.
div.p: DERNIER OWEN, I must hold my tongue.

div.head: 1383.—Friday, June 10, 1864.

div.head: 1384.—Tuesday, June 14, 1864.
div.p: SCOTLAND.—ROOKE the GRINDER, Grey, Bartletop, Staniforth, Black Bird, B. B. B. R. and Co. RETURN immediately, t’old Meston is takken bad.

div.head: 1385.—Friday, June 17, 1864.
div.p: GET the Paddington Dandy to visit the Country, and put up at A—— Hotel. He will find the French cuisine to his taste, and at his leisure be able to solve the enigmas of 59 and 60. All is discovered by a friend of the innocent, who forgets not her S—R—T friend, but can do nothing alone.

div.head: 1386.—Wednesday, June 22, 1864.
div.p: FIDES.—DOCUMENTS will AWAIT your Arrival at No. 3 on and after Tuesday next. Both of your letters to hand. (58.62) (171.53) (248.74) (152.79) (223.84) (25.21) (222.64) (132.74) James gone to Egypt instead.

div.head: 1387.—Thursday, June 23, July 2, 1864.

div.head: 1388.—Saturday, June 25, 1864.
div.p: FIDES.—Yours to hand. Unfortunately you mistook my last. He goes down on Monday to number two. If you can MEET there on Tuesday, he will doubtless be able to explain. div.head: 1389.—Tuesday, June 28, 1864.
div.p: IAM doomed to silence.

div.head: 1390.—Wednesday, June 29, 1864.
div.p: WHY doomed to silence? Is there any other means? Not there to-day.

div.head: 1391.—Saturday, July 2, 1864.
div.p: VBRUNSWICK A.

div.head: 1393.—Tuesday, July 5, 6, 1864.
div.p: A.E. I. With deep regret, No About.

div.head: 1394.—Tuesday, July 12, 1864.
div.p: IL n’y a rose sans épine! Mais, si de jeunesse on doit attendre beau colorès, Palleur qui marque une âme tendre, a ses attractions. Si —.— B., Saturday, July 9 1864.

div.head: 1395.—Thursday, July 14, 1864.
div.p: TO the LIVING DEAD, from Algeria.—Come, for now is the time.—A faithful One at the Cape.

div.head: 1399.—Friday, August 5, 1864.
div.p: 1.Yes. 2. Yes, favourable. 3. Yes. 4. Letter for S. J. H., P.O., St. Martin’s. 5. Yes. Safe, WRITE.

div.head: 1400.—Saturday, August 13, 1864.
div.p: TATTY.—The address as of old. All is unchanged, Henri. Proffered Jan. 15th, but refused.

div.head: 1401.—Saturday, August 20, 1864.
div.p: A.M.—“Canterbury.”

div.head: 1402.—Friday, August 26, 1864.
div.p: OBAN, August 28th, Oxford.

div.head: 1403.—Thursday, September 1, 1864.
div.p: M.N.—Ever the same. Wär ich ein Vögelein.

div.head: 1404.—Wednesday, September 7, 1864.
div.p: AUT TE AUT NIL?

div.head: 1406.—Friday, September 30, 1864.
div.p: FIDES.—Do not reply again until you hear from me. You shall have a note, as before, on Saturday morning. (58.62) (150.47) (23.28) (37.77) (161.98) (247.33) (80.9) (251.14).

div.head: 1407.—Tuesday, October 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 1864.
div.p: HEARTS are TRUMPS DOCTOR and I declare to win the odd trick. William Falley, Solicitor, Beaconsfield, and in London.

div.head: 1408.—Friday, October 7, 1864.
div.p: 100.Very beautiful. I am trying hard; but again, what seemed a chance has failed. Do WRITE soon.

div.head: 1409.—Saturday, October 8, 1864.
div.p: FIDES.—Yours received.—Be good enough to meet me as early as convenient, on Tuesday, that we may discuss matters. (109.104) (148.83) (129.50) (131.53) (157.20) (148.83) (58.62) (222.88) (134.68.69) (127.41).

div.head: 1410.—Tuesday, October 11, 1864.
div.p: E.B. W. D. V.—“The Pembroke Castle.” 20th, cheered and strengthened. Very thankful to you. To my life’s end I claim the right of a true friend, and trust you to let me know if ever I can be of use by word or deed; never feel painful or needless what would give me so much pleasure. F. for time Ναι ο Πατηρ ὁτι ὁυτως εγενετο ειδοκια εμπρωσθεν σον “Denique cœlum,” et de Britannia, et de India, æqualiter patet aula cœlestis.

div.head: 1411.—Monday, October 17, 1864.
div.p: FIDES.—I have not any communication from you this morning. When, and to what address shall I send the document you ask for in your P.S. of Thursday? It is delayed a week, so there is not the necessity for you to hasten your rejoinder (58.62) (164.17) (218.57) (250.86) (1) (2) (134.35) (58.52) (111.48) (P) (17.22) (194.7) (2) (197.18) (1) (249.80) (2) (44.36) (241.45).—Saturday, Oct. 15.

div.head: 1412.—Tuesday, October 18, 19, 20, 1864.
div.p: T—I. L—N.—“Flowrets are blooming.” “All that is wanting dear T—T. is you.” Ill and in trouble. Be merciful as you wish for mercy. Rely on secrecy, and pray communicate with L—Y. P—T.

div.head: 1413.—Saturday, October 22, 1864.
div.p: BONO.—Will be served.

div.p: FIDES.—Yours to hand this morning. I was consulted yesterday upon the question, and gave it decided approval. (100.33) (207.71) (142.37) (174.33) (154.30) (2) (73.62) (133.71) (199.91) (227.79) (48.6) (234.35) (265.16).—Thursday, 3rd Nov.

div.head: 1416.—Saturday, November 5, 1864.
div.p: RUNAWAY.—Yes, 21 or 31. Come to 41.

div.head: 1417.—Tuesday, November 8, 1864.
div.p: YORK in FUTURE.—They were mine. No chance of his ever seeing them, so do not be afraid. I think I see an opening soon.

div.head: 1418.—Monday, November 28, 1864.
div.p: C.C. C.—WAKE UP. TAKE.

div.head: 1419.—Monday, November 28, 1864.
div.p: ALPHA.—Neither you nor those Newcastle persons need entertain any personal fears whatever. You know I am not vindictive; and if under present circumstances you both leave me entirely alone, I will with my whole heart forgive and forget all past personal injuries. This is the only boon I ever will accept, and I am also fully determined never to give you (A) the information which you have tried to extort by annoyance.—K.

div.head: 1420.—Saturday, December 24, 1864.
div.p: L’ABBANDONATA.

div.head: 1421.—Friday, December 30, 1864.
div.p: IT is a DESPOTISM.—B.

div.head: 1422.—Tuesday, January 3, 1865.
div.p: 59.—Your letters frighten me a little. My brave one must overcome such dreadful fancies. Most anxious you should act at once, so that effects of probable failure may pass the sooner.—For ever.

div.head: 1423.—Thursday, January 5, 1865.
div.p: 59.—So often in pain! . . . Implicitly do I trust in my wife. But conceive no blind dislike for the best friend we have. It would be narrow-minded not to tolerate differences of opinion; and is it not enough that I should have adopted your fanaticism on this point as the religion of my life?

div.head: 1424.—Saturday, January 7, 1865.
div.p: L’ABBANDONATA—Traurig und allein.—P. d. V. R.

div.head: 1425.—Saturday, January 7, 1865.
div.p: YORK.—Do you want to do so with anybody else’s? So disappointed yesterday, but knew perfectly it was not your fault.—Ever.

div.head: 1426.—Wednesday, January 11, 1865.
div.p: 59.—Be explicit concerning any steps you wish taken. Failure probable in an effort here, but I think not very important.

div.head: 1427.—Thursday, January 12, 13, 1865.
div.p: PAEAN.—There is Codicil ——. .——. 06346.—“Custos rotulorum” 37. H. 8. C. T. Taken and acknowledged this day, the 11th of January, 1865.—Pollaky’s Private Inquiry-office, 13 Paddington-green, W.

div.head: 1428.—Friday, January 13, 1865.
div.p: 59.—Suspicious appearance to-day. . . . As I feared, but immediately begun at another. Want to speak.

div.head: 1433.—Wednesday, February 1, March 1, April 1, 1865.
div.p: QUITE by ACCIDENT.—Exhibition, 1851.

div.head: 1434.—Friday, February 3, 4, 1865.
div.p: BREAK BREAD AGAIN.—A bad father deserves to come to grief.

div.head: 1435.—Saturday, February 11, 14, 1865.
div.p: BUMPUS had fully foreseen importance in every point and will regard all the good advice; watch daily for report of events.

div.head: 1438.—Thursday, March 2, 14, 1865.
div.p: WE MET THEN for the Last Time.

div.head: 1439.—Thursday, March 2, 1865.
div.p: CARL . . . E MA . . . C.—Hope beats high that 12 of the 3rd will see a star in the ascendant.—R. R. APSLEY.

div.head: 1440.—Friday, March 3, 1865.
div.p: MASONIC.—Does Carlisle lose the bet to-day (the 3rd), at 12? The Burlington should decide, or Rotten-row if fine.

div.head: 1441.—Saturday, March 4, 1865.
div.p: WILL GOLDEN BROWN (M) look at the purple stain on the cross on the breast-plate of England, at Cramer’s.

div.head: 1442.—Saturday, March 4, 1865.
div.p: MASONIC.—The bet still holds good. Can it not be lost to-day (Saturday)? It is much desired, Masons all “good and true.” Burlington, about noon.

div.head: 1443.—Wednesday, March 15, 1865.
div.p: “WE met, then, for the last time.” Your sister was faithful to her promise, but you were not present. Feelings the same.

div.head: 1444.—Friday, March 17, 1865.
div.p: Z.B., 5a. If that is a rock of offence, remove it to 28 Red — — E. N.

div.p: 4.A. 3. D. 2.—THANKS; but it is too late, the book is out of my hands and must appear. Run no further risk on my account.—BELLE Boyd.

div.p: D.L. D. pour.—S. L.

div.head: 1450.—Wednesday, April 12, 1865.
div.p: G.L.—Is your promise forgotten or delayed? Do not be blinded by “acting.” Consummate art counterfeits nature.

div.p: TO INVALID.—Doubtless correct as to gold, A pair of gold spectacles in addition. The name is in the bag.
